C:\Users\AAAAA\Desktop\miliastra-game-template on 2026-09-27. That template has
since evolved: its documentation conventions, its shelves, and the rules it
ships have changed, and some of this repository's own notes were written
against older versions of both.

Treat the template as read-only reference. Do not edit it, do not copy its
product files in wholesale, and do not run anything inside it.

Your job is bounded. The scope is exactly these 74 Markdown files:
- AGENTS.md, CONTEXT.md, PRD.md
- every .md file under docs/project/
- every .md file under docs/guides/
- every .md file under docs/adr/

Nothing else in this repository is in scope. Read another file only when one of
the 74 points at it, and never edit one outside the scope.

Complete these deliverables, in order. Each is finite; when it is done, move to
the next. Do not expand the scope.

1. For each of the 7 index files in scope (docs/project/index.md,
   docs/project/building/index.md, docs/project/platform/index.md,
   docs/project/sessions/index.md,
   docs/project/building/phase0-protocols/index.md, docs/adr/index.md,
   docs/guides/index.md), make the index match its directory: every file that
   exists there is listed, and no listed file is absent.

2. In the five entry documents (AGENTS.md, CONTEXT.md, PRD.md,
   docs/project/index.md, docs/guides/index.md), make every repo-relative path
   resolve, or say plainly that the thing lives in the template and name the
   external path. A path that never existed in this repository is a defect.

3. In those same five documents, make every reference of the form
   "<file> § <heading>" name a heading that exists in that file.

4. Read the template's docs/project/index.md. Where its document conventions
   differ from this repository's, choose one side and record the choice in
   docs/project/index.md, in the section that states conventions. A note that
   the two differ, with no decision, does not finish this deliverable.

5. Write docs/plans/2026-10-24-template-resync/00-log.md. One row per thing you
   changed or deliberately did not change: what was wrong, why, which files
   changed, and status (changed / left alone, because ...). Every file you edit
   appears in a row.

6. Leave archive/, other games reference material/, docs/official-docs-mirror-*/
   and the template untouched. Do not create files outside docs/ and the
   repository root.

If a deliverable would take you outside the scope, record it as "left alone,
because ..." in the log and move to the next deliverable. That is the correct
end state for that item, not a gap to chase.

When all six deliverables are done, emit exactly one line of the form

BENCH-DONE <ISO-8601 timestamp>

as the last line of an assistant message that also states, in at most five
sentences, what you changed and what you knowingly left alone. After that line,
stop. Do not keep editing after declaring done.

# AGENTS.md

RACOONS (记忆焚化工) — "Remove Agent Context Overhead — Offload, Not Summarize." An open-source TypeScript library that keeps a coding agent's context healthy by removing provably useless content while it is fresh: capped oversized results, sealed failed-search episodes replaced by terse negative facts, closed episodes evicted whole and restorable by recall id. It never summarizes. The spec is `PRD-racoons.md` — read it before any implementation work. This repo does not contain the reference implementation; dsh-bot is the reference implementation and the live-test target — see `docs/reference-implementations.md`.

Do not add or reword a rule in this file. A new rule is a sentence you propose; the human lands it. Rules bind agents, not the human.

## Reading order

1. This file.
2. `docs/project/index.md` — the routing table; the conventions' home.
3. `docs/project/ref-glossary.md` — the vocabulary; use these terms, not their avoid-list synonyms.
4. `PRD-racoons.md` — the product spec (amended 2026-10-19: delay compaction ≥3×, stretch 10×).
5. `docs/reference-implementations.md` — before any work that touches dsh, dsh-bot, or live testing.
6. The `docs/guides/law-*.md` file that matches the work you are about to do.

## Issues and records law

- File a defect or task under `issue-tracker/open/` before the work; `NNN` is the highest existing number across open/resolved/deferred plus one; a state move is one atomic change; never delete a tracked issue file. (`docs/guides/law-editing-issue-files.md`)
- An ADR is a product decision, one decision per file, written before the change. IDs are permanent. Workplace rules are not ADRs. (`docs/guides/law-writing-an-adr.md`)
- Shelf law: `docs/specs/` is a rule that is still true. `docs/plans/<date>-<topic>/` is in-flight work and is not evidence. `docs/research/` is evidence and prior art — never a ruling. `archive/` is proof, written once, never required reading. `build/` and `scratchpad/` are disposable and never cited.
- Prefixes: `law-` is read before that kind of work; `ref-` is opened only when the task touches it; `work-` is never cited. A file's body caps at 250 lines (the imported PRD is excepted).

## Already broken in practice

- Citing `scratchpad/` or `build/` files as evidence — they are disposable by law.
- Copying from the dsh reference tree or dsh-bot prose. Adapted copying only: restructured, independently named, never textually identical. The reference tree never enters this repo, CI, or build (PRD §17).
- Running live dsh/LLM tests without the kill timer set at launch, with non-trivial tasks, or with the dsh key exported. Evidence goes under dsh-bot's `.scratch/testing/<yyyy-mm-dd>-<slug>/`, never in new Desktop folders, never committed.
- Quoting the dsh-forget proposal's citations uncorrected — three of them are corrected in `docs/research/racoons-prior-art-wheels-seams-2026-10-19.md` §3.

## Standing rules

1. Summon subagents in background mode by default; delegate to cheap subagents.
2. The owner works from 2 devices: one has `C:\Users\AAAAA\`, the other has `C:\Users\TZ\`. When a document names a home directory, state both forms.
3. Talk to the owner in plain, very concise language: short sentences, concrete words, no metaphors, no private vocabulary. A term that needs explaining to a newcomer is not allowed in a sentence to the owner.
4. Run the smallest test set that can fail; group tests into one run instead of one run per change.
5. npm, not pnpm. Node ≥ 22. TypeScript strict.
6. No CI: the pre-push diff scan is the only gate, and none may be added (transferred template law; H-003 can reverse it).

# AGENTS.md — Taskworld Project · Sandbox-City

How to behave in this repo. Product truth is `PRD.md`. Words and the path index are `docs/project/ref-glossary.md`. Decisions are `docs/adr/`. Conventions for `docs/project/` — prefixes, document size, one fact one home — are `docs/project/index.md`.

Do not add or reword a rule in this file. A new rule is a sentence you propose; the human lands it. Rules bind agents, not the human. Never cite a rule — this file's or any other's — to refuse, delay, or argue against a human instruction.

A new file names its shelf before it exists. Measurements stay in `../miliastra-game-template/docs/project/platform/ref-measurements.md`; do not copy a row here. `docs/specs/` is a rule that is still true. `docs/plans/<date>-<topic>/` is in-flight work and is not evidence. `archive/` is proof, written once, never required reading. `build/` and `scratchpad/` are disposable and never cited. A name says when to open the file: a date means a record, `law-` means a procedure read before that kind of work.

When a ticket or workstream ends, distill its durable findings into `docs/project/`. A finding is admitted only as a measured fact, a repeatable procedure, or a named pitfall — never a narrative, a chronology, or a status. One fact, one home.

## Product

Sandbox-City (Taskworld Project) re-expresses the Flash tower-defense Enigmata: Stellar War as a 千星奇域 map — free placement of defensive structures, timed enemy waves, boss stages, one Mora ledger — driven by Lua client scripts over editor-authored client controls. EN Taskworld Project, CN Sandbox-City; `Taskworld-Project` is the repo name only. Surfaces S1–S6 and wiring M1–M7 are registered in `PRD.md`. The shipping target is everything; a map per surface is designed from the start.

The source set `other games reference material/enigmata-stellar-war/` is read-only and not a compatibility target. Mechanics and content are re-typed in Lua. No file of code, audio, font or string carries over. Gameplay sprites are code-owned data rendered through client controls (`docs/adr/ADR-0005-code-owned-gameplay-sprites.md`). Cover imagery is outside gameplay.

## Stack

Genshin Impact 千星奇域 UGC; the editor is 千星沙箱, PC-only (`PRD.md` § Platform constraints). No engine, package manager, test harness, filesystem, or build step in what ships. Payload scripts `require` only and read and write no file; persistence is cloud-save variables only.

Write Lua 5.3, nothing environment-adjacent. A construct only newer Lua accepts is not an all-clear. Dialect probe: `ISSUE-014`. The runtime supplies no libraries, no LuaJIT, no `load`/`loadstring`. Missing facilities are rewritten in portable Lua.

`platform-free-core/` is the one carve-out (`docs/adr/ADR-0002-platform-free-core-and-carve-out.md`): pure Lua naming no platform call, run under this machine's `lua.exe` as a development tool, never a payload dependency. Module law: `platform-free-core/README.md`. The 5.1-safe subset is policed by `dev/lua-gate/`, not by that interpreter — local Lua 5.4.5 parses what the subset bans (`docs/project/building/ref-lua-subset-gate.md`). A local named exactly `oddx` miscompiles; rename and re-run before believing the failure. A green local run is arithmetic evidence only, never proof the payload loads.

A documented figure is never a designable number. Engine measurements live in `../miliastra-game-template/docs/project/platform/ref-measurements.md`. A number copied into this repo is stale. Design against a value you confirmed in the editor, and expect it to move.

## Contracts

- A surface's state machine owns phase and outcomes. The control layer only displays them. Logic inside a draw path is a defect.
- Settlement is event-driven. Mora changes on the settle event, never on a clock. Exactly one write seam (`PRD.md` F13, M2).
- Rewrite control text when the fact changes. Never rebuild a surface to change one number.
- Fragile areas — report, do not fix. A change names the invariant: the Mora ledger write (never negative, re-granted at stage start, forfeit on leave) and its save-key namespace; the phase owner (`PRD.md` M1); the structure, enemy, enhancement and stage tables in `PRD.md` § Content of record; the placement-capacity rule (`PRD.md` F4) — eight placed structures including the Command Base.

## Localization

EN and CN are co-equal, authored together. No player-facing literal in code or in an editor text field. Both entries of a key land in the same change. Parity is opening `locale/en.lua` and `locale/zh_cn.lua`. Never import the source game's locale files. Do not quote a remembered key total.

## Verification

The legibility gate (`PRD.md` NFR12) is a human judgement. An agent cannot pass it. Capture is a pre-check, never acceptance. Where you cannot play, say the requirement is unverified. Graceful degradation is `PRD.md` NFR18; the game plays with motion off (NFR13).

## Issues and decisions

File a defect with a failing check under `issue-tracker/open/` before the fix. Do not file a doc or process issue. Do not write a handover file. Numbering and moves: `docs/guides/law-editing-issue-files.md`. An issue file is never deleted.

ADRs are product and content decisions, written before the decision is implemented. Workplace rules are not ADRs. Convention: `docs/guides/law-writing-an-adr.md`. The live list is `docs/adr/index.md`.

`archive/` is proof, never required reading. Do not edit it and do not append inside it.

## Editing

No bulk replace and no tree-wide regex: both have corrupted UTF-8 and CN strings (千星奇域, 千星沙箱, 摩拉). After a multi-file edit, confirm each file still decodes as UTF-8.

Cite paths relative to the repo root. The one sibling path allowed is `../miliastra-game-template/docs/project/platform/ref-measurements.md`. A machine-local absolute needs `<!-- device-path: … -->` on that same block. `file:///` is never used.

One writer per file. A non-owner writes the exact wording into the owning ticket. One git writer per checkout; concurrent lanes may use separate worktrees. Commits are pathspec-limited. No history surgery in a shared checkout.

## Shell and the game

Every shell command has a positive timeout and does only what was asked. Never a watcher, dev server, REPL, or open-ended job. No CI, and do not add one.

Never kill the game process. Exit a playtest in-game: Esc, then 中断挑战, then 离开. Force-kill `YuanShen.exe` only when the game is frozen and that path does not work.

Publishing a map is a human action. Never submit or publish through the Sandbox, and never touch a published map. Push, PRs, tags, and write-scoped `gh` only when the human asks in this conversation.

From the Genshin main menu: Esc, scroll to the bottom, 我的奇域. Esc on an editor tab returns to the editor menu; Esc again toggles the left bar. The third button on that bar is the save-file manager. Turn logging on every time the editor opens, or the session writes no `.gia`: 千星沙箱 window, 窗口 → 日志, scroll 选择单位 to the bottom, tick 客户端脚本. Further click-paths are `docs/project/sessions/law-editor-sessions.md`, and only during a Sandbox session.

## Standing rules
1. Summon subagents in background mode by default.
2. Owner works from 2 devices: one has `C:\Users\AAAAA\`, the other has `C:\Users\TZ\`.
3. Never invent jargon, codenames, or project shorthand. Talk to the human in plain, very concise language, as if he has ADHD: short sentences, concrete words, no metaphors, no private vocabulary. A term that needs explaining to a newcomer is not allowed in a sentence to the owner.
4. Run the smallest test set that can fail. Do not run end-to-end tests when unit tests cover the change. Group tests into one run instead of starting one run per change.

</system-reminder>

2: 
3: One line per decision. **Hand-maintained** — there is no generator, so adding an ADR means adding its
4: row here. Convention: `docs/guides/law-writing-an-adr.md`.
5: 
6: The next number is derived by listing `docs/adr/`, never from this line.
7: 
8: Row grammar: the `Law` cell **mirrors that record's in-force `Law:` line verbatim** — never a summary,
9: no *Consequences* prose, no re-bolded clause (`docs/guides/law-writing-an-adr.md` § *File anatomy*).
10: A changed rule is edited in place in its record, so the cell always states what that ADR is now; where
11: a record carries a `Superseded-by`/`Supersedes` line, the cell adds that one plain cross-reference —
12: no dated qualifier, no amendment note.
13: 
14: | ID | Topic | Law |
15: | --- | --- | --- |
16: | ADR-0001 | naming | The product is named EN *Taskworld Project*, CN **Sandbox-City**; `Taskworld-Project` is the repo and code name, internal and never player-facing. |
17: | ADR-0002 | platform, layout | The platform-free core is Lua naming no platform call, control, save-variable runtime form, coordinate or cap; it may be organised per surface and per shared concern, runs only under this machine's interpreter as a development tool and never a payload dependency, and its 5.1-safe subset is enforced by a static gate module rather than by that runtime — whose 5.4.5 accepts every banned construct. *(superseded in part by ADR-0006 for the phase-gate conditioning clause only)* |
18: | ADR-0003 | rules, content | The source game's rules, content and data tables carry over as design seed and nothing else does — no line of code, no file of audio, font or string, and not the previous attempt's genshin-ts toolchain — with the seed corpus's `IMPL_05_DATA_TABLES.md` § *Appendix B* named as the conflict authority for its content figures. |
19: | ADR-0004 | art | Art is loaded into the map as editor image assets and never drawn at runtime, so it costs a budget rather than code; the salvaged example's runtime rect-explosion shape is rejected as the shipping shape, and which art source the project uses stays an open human decision. *(superseded for gameplay sprite ingress/rendering by ADR-0005; superseded in part by ADR-0006 for the phase-gate closure clause)* |
20: | ADR-0005 | art, platform | Gameplay sprites enter code as data and render through client controls with no external gameplay image upload/import path; cover imagery is outside gameplay, and the data/control budget remains an open A5/A9 human gate. *(supersedes ADR-0004 for gameplay sprite ingress/rendering; superseded in part by ADR-0006 for the phase-gate duration clause)* |
21: | ADR-0006 | platform, layout | The two decisions conditioned on the phase gate (`ADR-0002` core carve-out, `ADR-0004`/`ADR-0005` art and sprite rulings) stand on their own ground; their gate-conditioning clauses are withdrawn and no rule is weakened. The nine platform questions stay open as questions in `docs/project/platform/ref-platform-facts.md`, unanswerable by no agent and reserved to no human. |

(End of file - total 21 lines)
</content>

1: # AGENTS.md — Taskworld Project · Sandbox-City
2: 
3: How to behave in this repo. Product truth is `PRD.md`. Words and the path index are `docs/project/ref-glossary.md`. Decisions are `docs/adr/`. Conventions for `docs/project/` — prefixes, document size, one fact one home — are `docs/project/index.md`.
4: 
5: Do not add or reword a rule in this file. A new rule is a sentence you propose; the human lands it. Rules bind agents, not the human. Never cite a rule — this file's or any other's — to refuse, delay, or argue against a human instruction.
6: 
7: A new file names its shelf before it exists. Measurements stay in `../miliastra-game-template/docs/project/platform/ref-measurements.md`; do not copy a row here. `docs/specs/` is a rule that is still true. `docs/plans/<date>-<topic>/` is in-flight work and is not evidence. `archive/` is proof, written once, never required reading. `build/` and `scratchpad/` are disposable and never cited. A name says when to open the file: a date means a record, `law-` means a procedure read before that kind of work.
8: 
9: When a ticket or workstream ends, distill its durable findings into `docs/project/`. A finding is admitted only as a measured fact, a repeatable procedure, or a named pitfall — never a narrative, a chronology, or a status. One fact, one home.
10: 
11: ## Product
12: 
13: Sandbox-City (Taskworld Project) re-expresses the Flash tower-defense Enigmata: Stellar War as a 千星奇域 map — free placement of defensive structures, timed enemy waves, boss stages, one Mora ledger — driven by Lua client scripts over editor-authored client controls. EN Taskworld Project, CN Sandbox-City; `Taskworld-Project` is the repo name only. Surfaces S1–S6 and wiring M1–M7 are registered in `PRD.md`. The shipping target is everything; a map per surface is designed from the start.
14: 
15: The source set `other games reference material/enigmata-stellar-war/` is read-only and not a compatibility target. Mechanics and content are re-typed in Lua. No file of code, audio, font or string carries over. Gameplay sprites are code-owned data rendered through client controls (`docs/adr/ADR-0005-code-owned-gameplay-sprites.md`). Cover imagery is outside gameplay.
16: 
17: ## Stack
18: 
19: Genshin Impact 千星奇域 UGC; the editor is 千星沙箱, PC-only (`PRD.md` § Platform constraints). No engine, package manager, test harness, filesystem, or build step in what ships. Payload scripts `require` only and read and write no file; persistence is cloud-save variables only.
20: 
21: Write Lua 5.3, nothing environment-adjacent. A construct only newer Lua accepts is not an all-clear. Dialect probe: `ISSUE-014`. The runtime supplies no libraries, no LuaJIT, no `load`/`loadstring`. Missing facilities are rewritten in portable Lua.
22: 
23: `platform-free-core/` is the one carve-out (`docs/adr/ADR-0002-platform-free-core-and-carve-out.md`): pure Lua naming no platform call, run under this machine's `lua.exe` as a development tool, never a payload dependency. Module law: `platform-free-core/README.md`. The 5.1-safe subset is policed by `dev/lua-gate/`, not by that interpreter — local Lua 5.4.5 parses what the subset bans (`docs/project/building/ref-lua-subset-gate.md`). A local named exactly `oddx` miscompiles; rename and re-run before believing the failure. A green local run is arithmetic evidence only, never proof the payload loads.
24: 
25: A documented figure is never a designable number. Engine measurements live in `../miliastra-game-template/docs/project/platform/ref-measurements.md`. A number copied into this repo is stale. Design against a value you confirmed in the editor, and expect it to move.
26: 
27: ## Contracts
28: 
29: - A surface's state machine owns phase and outcomes. The control layer only displays them. Logic inside a draw path is a defect.
30: - Settlement is event-driven. Mora changes on the settle event, never on a clock. Exactly one write seam (`PRD.md` F13, M2).
31: - Rewrite control text when the fact changes. Never rebuild a surface to change one number.
32: - Fragile areas — report, do not fix. A change names the invariant: the Mora ledger write (never negative, re-granted at stage start, forfeit on leave) and its save-key namespace; the phase owner (`PRD.md` M1); the structure, enemy, enhancement and stage tables in `PRD.md` § Content of record; the placement-capacity rule (`PRD.md` F4) — eight placed structures including the Command Base.
33: 
34: ## Localization
35: 
36: EN and CN are co-equal, authored together. No player-facing literal in code or in an editor text field. Both entries of a key land in the same change. Parity is opening `locale/en.lua` and `locale/zh_cn.lua`. Never import the source game's locale files. Do not quote a remembered key total.
37: 
38: ## Verification
39: 
40: The legibility gate (`PRD.md` NFR12) is a human judgement. An agent cannot pass it. Capture is a pre-check, never acceptance. Where you cannot play, say the requirement is unverified. Graceful degradation is `PRD.md` NFR18; the game plays with motion off (NFR13).
41: 
42: ## Issues and decisions
43: 
44: File a defect with a failing check under `issue-tracker/open/` before the fix. Do not file a doc or process issue. Do not write a handover file. Numbering and moves: `docs/guides/law-editing-issue-files.md`. An issue file is never deleted.
45: 
46: ADRs are product and content decisions, written before the decision is implemented. Workplace rules are not ADRs. Convention: `docs/guides/law-writing-an-adr.md`. The live list is `docs/adr/index.md`.
47: 
48: `archive/` is proof, never required reading. Do not edit it and do not append inside it.
49:

Do not add or reword a rule in this file. A new rule is a sentence you propose; the human lands it. Rules bind agents, not the human. Never cite a rule — this file's or any other's — to refuse, delay, or argue against a human instruction.

A new file names its shelf before it exists. Measurements stay in `../miliastra-game-template/docs/project/platform/ref-measurements.md`; do not copy a row here. `docs/specs/` is a rule that is still true. `docs/plans/<date>-<topic>/` is in-flight work and is not evidence. `archive/` is proof, written once, never required reading. `build/` and `scratchpad/` are disposable and never cited. A name says when to open the file: a date means a record, `law-` means a procedure read before that kind of work.

When a ticket or workstream ends, distill its durable findings into `docs/project/`. A finding is admitted only as a measured fact, a repeatable procedure, or a named pitfall — never a narrative, a chronology, or a status. One fact, one home.
## Product

Sandbox-City (Taskworld Project) re-expresses the Flash tower-defense Enigmata: Stellar War as a 千星奇域 map — free placement of defensive structures, timed enemy waves, boss stages, one Mora ledger — driven by Lua client scripts over editor-authored client controls. EN Taskworld Project, CN Sandbox-City; `Taskworld-Project` is the repo name only. Surfaces S1–S6 and wiring M1–M7 are registered in `PRD.md`. The shipping target is everything; a map per surface is designed from the start.

The source set `other games reference material/enigmata-stellar-war/` is read-only and not a compatibility target. Mechanics and content are re-typed in Lua. No file of code, audio, font or string carries over. Gameplay sprites are code-owned data rendered through client controls (`docs/adr/ADR-0005-code-owned-gameplay-sprites.md`). Cover imagery is outside gameplay.
## Stack

Genshin Impact 千星奇域 UGC; the editor is 千星沙箱, PC-only (`PRD.md` § Platform constraints). No engine, package manager, test harness, filesystem, or build step in what ships. Payload scripts `require` only and read and write no file; persistence is cloud-save variables only.

Write Lua 5.3, nothing environment-adjacent. A construct only newer Lua accepts is not an all-clear. Dialect probe: `ISSUE-014`. The runtime supplies no libraries, no LuaJIT, no `load`/`loadstring`. Missing facilities are rewritten in portable Lua.

A local named exactly `oddx` miscompiles; rename and re-run before believing the failure. A green local run is arithmetic evidence only, never proof the payload loads.

A documented figure is never a designable number. Engine measurements live in `../miliastra-game-template/docs/project/platform/ref-measurements.md`. A number copied into this repo is stale. Design against a value you confirmed in the editor, and expect it to move.

- Settlement is event-driven. Mora changes on the settle event, never on a clock. Exactly one write seam (`PRD.md` F13, M2).
- Rewrite control text when the fact changes. Never rebuild a surface to change one number.

- Fragile areas — report, do not fix. 1: # PRD — Taskworld Project · Sandbox-City
2: 
3: This file is product truth: every id cited elsewhere — surfaces, requirements, NFRs, posture rows, standing rules, open decisions — resolves here.
4: 
5: ## 1. Product statement
6: 
7: The player defends one open field: they place a handful of structures with their own hand, watch a timed enemy wave come at them, spend the Mora those kills returned on the next structure or the next upgrade, and finish the stage against a boss — in one sitting, on PC, alone. It is a 千星奇域 (Miliastra Wonderland) map driven by Lua client scripts and editor-authored client controls; its code name is `Taskworld-Project` (internal, never player-facing). What makes it worth playing is how much is forced into a few choices: eight placements and one currency force a real decision every intermission, and the five-stage campaign teaches that decision rather than rationing it out. The content set of record is the reduced set of section 7: 8 structures, 18 enemies, 5 stages, 12 enhancements, 6 talents, 8 items, 7 achievements.
8: 
9: ## 2. Platform
10: 
11: The stack, editor constraints and platform caveats live in `AGENTS.md` (Stack and platform); this document designs inside 5.1's constraints and waits on 5.2's assumptions.
12: 
13: ## 3. Goals and non-goals
14: 
15: ### 3.1 Goals
16: 
17: A goal is what a good session looks like; each is checkable by playing, and each is measured by the rows named beside it.
18: 
19: | # | Goal | Measured by |
20: | --- | --- | --- |
21: | G1 | A stranger clears Stage 1 on their first attempt and understands why if they lose. | F5, F12, F23, F29 |
22: | G2 | Every Mora movement is visible as a fact the moment it happens — the player can always say what they can afford. | F13-F21, NFR6, NFR7 |
23: | G3 | The build decision differs per stage: the roster, capacity and unlock chain force a different field each time. | F4-F11, F34 |
24: | G4 | A boss stage reads as a distinct fight — the phase flip is legible and winnable with prep, not with twitch. | F28, F9, F31 |
25: | G5 | Progress outlives the session: stages, stars, talents and achievements read back on the next visit, or degrade honestly. | F35-F39, NFR16 |
26: 
27: ### 3.2 Non-goals
28: 
29: Named so nobody helpfully adds them later; each is out of scope for v1 with its reason.
30: 
31: - No multiplayer, no co-op, no shared stake: no server authority exists to arbitrate one, and the stake of a run is the player's own (R3, D3).
32: - No premium currency, no gacha, no purchase path, no payout of any kind (pillar 3, N1, N2).
33: - No tile grid, no maze-building constraint, no terrain cost: the field is continuous and open (`other games reference material/enigmata-stellar-war/02_MAP_AND_BUILDING.md`); a grid would be a different game.
34: - No external gameplay image upload/import path and no text-canvas composition; gameplay sprites are code-owned data rendered through client controls (N5, D2).
35: - No ported Flash code, no genshin-ts/TypeScript pipeline, no node-graph logic for v1 mechanics: the code examples in the seed corpus (the previous attempt's design documents) are read with that caveat; logic is re-typed as Lua client scripts.
36: - No endless mode, no difficulty tiers beyond the recorded Normal pacing, no stage 6: out of scope, and only a human decision adds them.
37: - No persistence of in-stage state — balance, placed structures, wave index: a stage is a transaction (F39).
38: - No audio, fonts or 3D model content in v1 (N4, D1): the game must be fully playable silent (NFR13, NFR14).
39: - No mobile authoring or mobile acceptance target: the editor is PC-only (5.1); play on mobile is a look.
40: 
41: ## 4. Product pillars
42: 
43: The small set of promises every design decision is checked against.
44: 
45: 1. Readable command — the field reads as facts, not as motion. If a player cannot tell phase, balance, wave and threat apart at a glance, the surface is re-scoped, not animated harder.
46: 2. One economy, one owner — the Mora (摩拉) ledger is one number changed by named events at one seam (F13); no display path, timer or animation may mint or burn it (NFR6, NFR10).
47: 3. Economy posture — no real-money or platform-currency path anywhere: cosmetic-only stakes, no purchase path, no payout of any kind. Weaken it only by a human decision recorded in its own N row and, if it changes architecture, its own ADR.
48: 
49: ## 5. Platform constraints
50: 
51: ### 5.1 What the build must live inside
52: 
53: | Constraint | Consequence for this product |
54: | --- | --- |
55: | Logic is Lua client scripts, driving client controls authored in the editor. | The whole game is scripts plus control layouts. No engine, no framework, no build step, no platform libraries or vendor modules at runtime: a facility the runtime does not supply is rewritten in portable Lua (`AGENTS.md`, Stack and platform). |
56: | Client-local and server-side are separate domains. | Single-player logic may sit client-local; anything whose outcome must match for all players lives in a server-side graph. Nothing shared-stake is designed before the multiplayer decision (R3, D3). |
57: | The simultaneous-visible-control budget is the binding constraint. | All surfaces share one visible-control budget; hiding a whole group is the only relief valve, and whether a script may do it is A7. If it may not, the split-map fallback (section 8.3) is the plan, not an emergency. |
58: | Gameplay sprites are code-owned data rendered through client controls. | No external gameplay image upload/import path exists. The measured sprite-data and control capacity lives in `../miliastra-game-template/docs/project/platform/ref-measurements.md`; design against it. Cover imagery is outside gameplay. |
59: | Persistence is cloud-save variables only. No filesystem, no file I/O; whether `require` spans files is unresolved. | Persistent state is a variable with a capacity budget; a key registry with version stamps is needed before the first key is written (NFR16); save scope is A8. |
60: | Caps are documented, unit-less and scope-unconfirmed; the editor is PC-only. | Every printed cap digit is documentation, never a designable number — each is an early verification task (5.2), and layouts are designed against confirmed answers only. Playtesting on mobile is a look, not an edit. |
61: 
62: ### 5.2 Platform facts and open questions
63:

66: ## 6. Functional requirements
67: 
68: The acceptance column is a human instruction, not a test: a person can pass or fail the row in 千星沙箱 by doing what the row says, on the row's surface, with no tooling attached. What an agent may verify is narrow — arithmetic, wave ordering, AI policy and economy totals, executed in `platform-free-core/` under the local interpreter; no agent may claim that a screen reads, that a face is legible, that a layout fits, that a control budget held, or that persistence worked across a real session (`AGENTS.md`, Visual verification). Requirement IDs are append-only: a withdrawn item keeps its number.
69: 
70: ID conventions: bare, dot-free identifiers, each in one registry — F functional requirement (6.1); G goal (3.1); N product posture row (6.5); NFR non-functional requirement (6.4); R standing rule (6.6); A platform assumption (5.2); D open product decision (6.7); S surface (6.2); M wiring piece (6.3). IDs are never reused for a different meaning.

172: 
173: | # | Requirement | Why it is here |
174: | --- | --- | --- |
175: | NFR1 | No player-facing literal is hardcoded — not in a script, not typed into a control's text field. Every visible string is a key with both locale entries. | A literal is invisible to the second locale and unfixable in the field. |
176: | NFR2 | A missing key is a defect with a severity, never a fallback. A missing entry in one language blocks the change that introduced the key. | "EN landed, CN later" is how a bilingual product decays into a monolingual one. |
177: | NFR3 | The Mora balance is never negative (F15), and no code path may write a negative value to it. | Fragile area: the ledger. |
178: | NFR4 | A stage's starting Mora is always re-granted (F16); no balance ever arrives from persistence. | Fragile area: re-grant at zero — a stale save must never be able to lock a player out of their own run. |
179: | NFR5 | Leaving mid-stage forfeits the in-stage ledger and everything bought with it (F39). | Fragile area: forfeit on leave — the alternative is save-scumming the economy. |
180: | NFR6 | Settlement is event-driven. Mora moves on a named event; no clock, tick or animation advances economy state. | A clock-driven economy double-pays whenever cadence changes — and cadence is A2, i.e. unknown. |
181: | NFR7 | A readout changes by rewriting that one control's content when its fact changes. Rebuilding a surface to update one number is a defect. | Rebuilds spend the visible-control budget (A5/A7) and stutter the layout for no information. |
182: | NFR8 | No game rule is computed inside an animation or draw path. | Where A2 is unanswered, that path may not run at all; and a rule that only animates is unauditable. |
183: | NFR9 | Randomness is RNG in, decision out: every shuffle, drop roll and AI choice takes an order or seed and returns a decision. Same seeded input plays identically. | The only determinism a human can check by eye, and the only way a numeric core can be cited as evidence. |

247: ### 7.2 Cadence and economy constants

268: 
269: | ID | Enhancement | Cat | Cap | baseCost | costScale | Per level |
270: | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
271: | 1 | Sharpened Edge | ATK | 5 | 300 | 200 | +12% tower damage |
272: | 2 | Armor Shredder | ATK | 3 | 500 | 300 | ignore 5 flat armour |
273: | 3 | Critical Eye | ATK | 5 | 400 | 200 | +5% crit, 2× on crit |
274: | 4 | Fortified Plating | HP | 5 | 200 | 150 | +10% structure HP |

284: ### 7.4 Enemies, stages and waves
285: 
286: Enemy roster: 18 types — trash 100-104, standard 110-114, elite 120-122, flying 130-132, boss 150-151 — with HP, speed, attack, armour, Mora reward and behaviour per the seed corpus's data model. Bosses: 150 Azar — Star Devourer, 3000 HP, armour 10, reward 500, two phases, escorts and nova under 50% HP; 151 Krohn — Infernal Forge, 5000 HP, armour 15, reward 800, two phases. 296: ### 7.5 Talents and items
297:

300: Eight items: three Mora pouches (50 / 150 / 500), Attack Elixir, Swift Tonic, Aether Charm, Storm Lord's Wrath, Shadow Barrier; drop weights by enemy tier per the seed corpus's items doc (`DESIGN_UGC_07_ITEMS_TALENTS.md`).

302: ### 7.6 Rank and achievements
303: 
304: Rank thresholds 0 / 500 / 1500 / 4000 / 10000 EXP, per-run only; the top tier's compound multipliers are ×1.38 HP, ×1.44 damage, ×1.50 range. Seven achievements pay 500 / 2000 / 1000 / 1000 / 1500 / 2000 / 5000 Mora once each, on their named events (F37).
305: 
306: ### 7.7 Terms and strings
307: 
308: - `CONTEXT.md` is the term authority; the seed corpus's replacement glossary (`docs/plans/2026-05-27-previous-attempt-design-corpus/GLOSSARY_REPLACEMENTS.md`) is a candidate map adopted term by term, never wholesale.
309: - Every player-visible string is one key with an authored EN and an authored CN entry created in the same change (F40, NFR1, NFR2); the locale files are `locale/en.lua` and `locale/zh_cn.lua`, and the key count's home is `docs/project/building/ref-locale-denominator.md`.
310: - Never import the source game's or the previous attempt's locale files: agreed terminology is the reference; keys, layout and accessor never are.
311: 
312: ## 8. Phasing, exit criteria and the split-map fallback
313: 
314: ### 8.1 Phasing
315: 
316: - Phase 0 — a short investigation. It settles the open questions and builds almost nothing. Measure the open platform questions in writing (one research issue each), run the test procedures in `docs/project/building/phase0-protocols/`, record every measured figure together with the work pass that measured it, and choose one of two routes: a single map, or the split-map fallback. Close the open decisions (D1, D2, D7) to the extent a human will; the platform-free core (the economy code, the tables, the wave scheduler and the random-number generator) is organised and exercised during Phase 0.
317: - Phase 1 — build the surfaces in parallel. One surface per owner, no two owners touching the same files, and nothing published in this phase — a half-built hub is not a map. Order does not matter; the wiring (M1-M7) is integrated last, and the integration owner is responsible for those wiring rows.
318: - Phase 2 — integrate, and publish once. Publication is one event, allowed only when the whole set passes (8.2); the publishing checklist is handed to the human, who alone publishes.
319: 
320: ### 8.2 Whole-set exit criteria
321: 
322: The set a human reads before consenting to publication. Every row is pass/fail by playing; no row may be marked passed on the strength of an agent's own mockup.
323: 
324: 1. Every 6.2 surface row passes its acceptance check and its NFR12 gate on the real map, in both locales.
325: 2. Every 6.3 wiring row passes: one ledger (M2), one phase owner (M1), one persisted key registry (M4).
326: 3. Every F-row's acceptance has been walked by a person who did not write it, in order, S1 to S6.
327: 4. NFR1-NFR18 hold, or name their exception in writing; NFR12's gate has a dated human verdict beside it.
328: 5. The platform questions of 5.2 are measured, each resolving into an ADR where the answer changes architecture — an unanswered question that a row depends on is a blocked publication, not a risk note.
329: 6. Both locale key sets are identical, verified by opening both files, and the count is stamped at its home (`docs/project/building/ref-locale-denominator.md`).
330: 7. D1, D2 and D7 are decided; where D2 is still open, no final gameplay sprite-data set claim may be made and the set fails.
331: 8. A playtest path exists for all five stages end to end, silent and motion-off (NFR13, NFR14).
332: 9. No row in this file cites an unconfirmed platform figure as its basis (R1, NFR17).
333: 10. The creator-facing policy reading has happened by a human, and its name, version and date are recorded.
334: 
335: ### 8.3 The split-map fallback — designed for from the start
336: 
337: If A7 answers that a script may not show and hide whole control groups, or if A5's confirmed count cannot hold S1-S6 at once, each surface becomes its own map with S1 as the entry point. Planned from the start, not used as a last resort:
338: 
339: - The economy stays in-run either way: Mora is session-scoped (F21), so the split never splits the balance; what the split threatens is read-back, and A8 decides whether one persisted key set survives across maps. If A8 answers per map, the progression data families (F36) must be given a new place or the campaign restructured — a scope change decided by a human, never absorbed silently.
340: - Cost named in advance: the phase driver (M1), ledger seam (M2) and the locale lookup (M7) are duplicated per map, and every hand-off between maps becomes an authored entry point rather than a show/hide.
341: - The exit criterion that changes: 8.2 row 1 is then checked per map, and row 5's A5/A7/A8 answers are the evidence attached to the decision.

lines.text: # PRD — Taskworld Project · Sandbox-City
This file is product truth: every id cited elsewhere — surfaces, requirements, NFRs, posture rows, standing rules, open decisions — resolves here.
## 1. Product statement

The player defends one open field: they place a handful of structures with their own hand, watch a timed enemy wave come at them, spend the Mora those kills returned on the next structure or the next upgrade, and finish the stage against a boss — in one sitting, on PC, alone. It is a 千星奇域 (Miliastra Wonderland) map driven by Lua client scripts and editor-authored client controls; its code name is `Taskworld-Project` (internal, never player-facing). What makes it worth playing is how much is forced into a few choices: eight placements and one currency force a real decision every intermission, and the five-stage campaign teaches that decision rather than rationing it out. The content set of record is the reduced set of section 7: 8 structures, 18 enemies, 5 stages, 12 enhancements, 6 talents, 8 items, 7 achievements.
## 2. Platform
The stack, editor constraints and platform caveats live in `AGENTS.md` (Stack and platform); this document designs inside 5.1's constraints and waits on 5.2's assumptions.
## 3. Goals and non-goals
### 3.1 Goals
A goal is what a good session looks like; each is checkable by playing, and each is measured by the rows named beside it.
| # | Goal | Measured by |
| G1 | A stranger clears Stage 1 on their first attempt and understands why if they lose. | F5, F12, F23, F29 |
| G2 | Every Mora movement is visible as a fact the moment it happens — the player can always say what they can afford. | F13-F21, NFR6, NFR7 |
| G3 | The build decision differs per stage: the roster, capacity and unlock chain force a different field each time. | F4-F11, F34 |
| G4 | A boss stage reads as a distinct fight — the phase flip is legible and winnable with prep, not with twitch. | F28, F9, F31 |
| G5 | Progress outlives the session: stages, stars, talents and achievements read back on the next visit, or degrade honestly. | F35-F39, NFR16 |
### 3.2 Non-goals
Named so nobody helpfully adds them later; each is out of scope for v1 with its reason.
- No multiplayer, no co-op, no shared stake: no server authority exists to arbitrate one, and the stake of a run is the player's own (R3, D3).
- No premium currency, no gacha, no purchase path, no payout of any kind (pillar 3, N1, N2).

- No tile grid, no maze-building constraint, no terrain cost: the field is continuous and open (`other games reference material/enigmata-stellar-war/02_MAP_AND_BUILDING.md`); a grid would be a different game.
- No external gameplay image upload/import path and no text-canvas composition; gameplay sprites are code-owned data rendered through client controls (N5, D2).

- No ported Flash code, no genshin-ts/TypeScript pipeline, no node-graph logic for v1 mechanics: the code examples in the seed corpus (the previous attempt's design documents) are read with that caveat; logic is re-typed as Lua client scripts.
- No endless mode, no difficulty tiers beyond the recorded Normal pacing, no stage 6: out of scope, and only a human decision adds them.
- No persistence of in-stage state — balance, placed structures, wave index: a stage is a transaction (F39).
- No audio, fonts or 3D model content in v1 (N4, D1): the game must be fully playable silent (NFR13, NFR14).
- No mobile authoring or mobile acceptance target: the editor is PC-only (5.1); play on mobile is a look.
## 4. Product pillars
The small set of promises every design decision is checked against.
1. Readable command — the field reads as facts, not as motion. If a player cannot tell phase, balance, wave and threat apart at a glance, the surface is re-scoped, not animated harder.
2. One economy, one owner — the Mora (摩拉) ledger is one number changed by named events at one seam (F13); no display path, timer or animation may mint or burn it (NFR6, NFR10).

3. Economy posture — no real-money or platform-currency path anywhere: cosmetic-only stakes, no purchase path, no payout of any kind. Weaken it only by a human decision recorded in its own N row and, if it changes architecture, its own ADR.
## 5. Platform constraints
### 5.1 What the build must live inside
| Constraint | Consequence for this product |

| Logic is Lua client scripts, driving client controls authored in the editor. | The whole game is scripts plus control layouts. No engine, no framework, no build step, no platform libraries or vendor modules at runtime: a facility the runtime does not supply is rewritten in portable Lua (`AGENTS.md`, Stack and platform). |

| Client-local and server-side are separate domains. | Single-player logic may sit client-local; anything whose outcome must match for all players lives in a server-side graph. Nothing shared-stake is designed before the multiplayer decision (R3, D3). |

| The simultaneous-visible-control budget is the binding constraint. | All surfaces share one visible-control budget; hiding a whole group is the only relief valve, and whether a script may do it is A7. If it may not, the split-map fallback (section 8.3) is the plan, not an emergency. |

| Gameplay sprites are code-owned data rendered through client controls. | No external gameplay image upload/import path exists. The measured sprite-data and control capacity lives in `../miliastra-game-template/docs/project/platform/ref-measurements.md`; design against it. Cover imagery is outside gameplay. |

| Persistence is cloud-save variables only. No filesystem, no file I/O; whether `require` spans files is unresolved. | Persistent state is a variable with a capacity budget; a key registry with version stamps is needed before the first key is written (NFR16); save scope is A8. |

| Caps are documented, unit-less and scope-unconfirmed; the editor is PC-only. | Every printed cap digit is documentation, never a designable number — each is an early verification task (5.2), and layouts are designed against confirmed answers only. Playtesting on mobile is a look, not an edit. |
### 5.2 Platform facts and open questions

What the device has actually measured — layout, the tick, per-control text, runtime control creation, the caps and the sprite budget — lives in `../miliastra-game-template/docs/project/platform/ref-measurements.md`, and what remains unknown — cross-session save, group show/hide, cloud-save scope — is kept as open questions in `docs/project/platform/ref-platform-facts.md`. Design against the measured rows in ENGINE.md; the open questions have one `Type: research` issue each, and each resolves into an ADR where the answer changes architecture. The earlier practice of treating these as assumptions to be gated is retired (see `AGENTS.md`, Platform facts and open questions).
## 6. Functional requirements

The acceptance column is a human instruction, not a test: a person can pass or fail the row in 千星沙箱 by doing what the row says, on the row's surface, with no tooling attached. What an agent may verify is narrow — arithmetic, wave ordering, AI policy and economy totals, executed in `platform-free-core/` under the local interpreter; no agent may claim that a screen reads, that a face is legible, that a layout fits, that a control budget held, or that persistence worked across a real session (`AGENTS.md`, Visual verification). Requirement IDs are append-only: a withdrawn item keeps its number.

ID conventions: bare, dot-free identifiers, each in one registry — F functional requirement (6.1); G goal (3.1); N product posture row (6.5); NFR non-functional requirement (6.4); R standing rule (6.6); A platform assumption (5.2); D open product decision (6.7); S surface (6.2); M wiring piece (6.3). IDs are never reused for a different meaning.
### 6.1 Requirements F1-F40
Placement and the field.
| # | [S] | Requirement | Acceptance — checkable by playing |

| F1 | S3 | Structures may be placed at any authored buildable position of the open field; the position is continuous, not snapped to a grid. | Place two turrets at visibly different, non-grid-aligned points; both stay where set for the rest of the stage. |

| F2 | S3 | Placement is a two-tap act: choose a structure type, then designate a field position; a cancel path returns to the roster without spending. | Tap-cancel after selecting but before designating: balance unchanged, no structure on the field. |
| F3 | S3 | Placement and sell-back are accepted only in the PREP/BUILD phase. | Attempt both during COMBAT: refused, with the reason shown, and the balance unchanged. |

| F4 | S2 | Placement capacity: at most 8 placed structures including the Command Base (Content of record), raisable only by the recorded capacity enhancement (F18). | Fill to capacity, attempt one more: refused with the capacity reason; capacity reads 8/8 before the attempt. |

| F5 | S3 | Every refusal names its reason from a closed set — capacity, insufficient Mora, outside the build zone, position occupied — as a keyed string in both locales. | Trigger all four refusals in one stage; four different messages, none blank, none a raw key. |

| F6 | S3 | The buildable roster is exactly the seven buildable structure types of Content of record at their recorded costs, HP, damage, fire interval and range; the Command Base is authored into the field and never purchasable. | Open the roster: seven entries, each showing the recorded cost; the Command Base is absent from it and present on the field. |

| F7 | S2 | Each structure fights by its recorded table row — single target, pierce (2), splash with burn (3), slow (4), homing volley (7) — with no per-frame recomputation of authored data. | Watch one wave pass a mixed line; each tower's visible effect matches its row (splash hits more than one, the ray slows, the blaster pierces armor). |

| F8 | S2 | Flying enemies (Content of record, types 130-132) may be engaged only by the anti-air set 1, 2 and 7. | Bring a flying wave against a line with no anti-air: nothing engages the flyers; add one Arcane Turret and it does. |

| F9 | S2 | Mora Vault accrues Mora on the economy accrual beat (Content of record) at the recorded rate, at most 3 vaults active, and only while the phase is COMBAT or BOSS. | Two stages, one with 3 vaults one with none: the vaulted balance climbs during combat and is flat during PREP/BUILD and after the last wave. |

| F10 | S2 | Ward Barrier blocks ground pathing and takes fire in place of what is behind it, and grants the recorded resistance to adjacent structures; flyers ignore it entirely. | Ground waves stall at the barrier and chew it instead of the towers behind it; a flyer flies straight past the same barrier. |
| F11 | S3 | Magic Missile Array is purchasable only after Stage 3 is cleared. | Locked in S1-S3 with the reason shown; present and buyable in S4. |

| F12 | S2 | The Command Base holds the recorded HP, cannot be sold, relocated or repaired by spend, and its destruction ends the stage in defeat at once. | Let a wave through with no defenses: the run ends the moment the base falls, and the results surface says why. |
The Mora economy.
| # | [M] | Requirement | Acceptance — checkable by playing |

| F13 | M2 | Exactly one place changes the Mora balance — the ledger seam M2. Every source and sink in this section routes through it and nowhere else. | Play a full stage and read the balance history: every movement is one of the named events in F14; there is no unexplained drift. |

| F14 | M2 | The ledger's sources are: kill reward (F19), vault accrual (F9), item pickup (F32), stage-clear bonus (F20), achievement reward (F37), sell-back (F17). Its sinks are: structure purchase (F6), enhancement purchase (F18), talent activation (F31). Nothing else mints or burns Mora. | Enumerate a session's movements against that list; no seventh source and no fourth sink appears. |

| F15 | M2 | The balance is never negative and never fractional: a purchase whose cost exceeds the balance is refused before the seam, and every credit is an integer. | Spam-buy the most expensive item until refused; the balance stops at 0 or the remainder and never reads below zero. |

| F16 | M2 | A stage always begins by granting its recorded starting Mora (Content of record) — a fresh session, a retry and a return from the hub all re-grant it. No balance is ever read out of persistence. | Start, abandon and restart Stage 3: the opening balance is the recorded figure each time, never a stale one. |

| F17 | M2 | Sell-back returns 50% of that structure's purchase cost, integer-divided (rounded down), in PREP/BUILD only; enhancement spend on a sold structure is not refunded. | Sell a 350-cost mortar: +175; sell one that carried enhancement spend and the enhancement cost stays spent. |

| F18 | M2 | Enhancements: 12 rows in 6 categories (Content of record), purchasable only in PREP/BUILD and INTERMISSION. Cost of level n = `baseCost + costScale × (n − 1)`; each category caps at its recorded level; effects apply as computed multipliers over authored base stats, never by mutating authored data. Capacity extension raises F4's cap by the recorded amount per level. | Buy the same enhancement to its cap and stop: the button reads capped; the tower's damage recomputes from base × recorded per-level factor. |

| F19 | M2 | Kill reward pays on the kill event, at the recorded figure for that enemy, adjusted only by the recorded rank and economy multipliers, integer. | Clear a wave twice with the same seeded order: identical totals; adding Mora Amplifier raises the total by its recorded factor and nothing else changes. |

| F20 | M2 | The stage-clear bonus follows the ratified figure set of Content of record and is paid on the VICTORY event. Intermission pays no bonus at all. | Clear Stage 1: the results readout shows the recorded bonus; between waves 1 and 2 the balance moves only from kills and vaults. |

| F21 | M2 | The in-stage ledger is session-scoped: nothing about it — balance, purchases, earned rank — travels to the next stage or the next visit. | Clear S1 rich, open S2: the opening balance is S2's grant, not S1's remainder. |
Phases, waves and combat.
| # | [M] | Requirement | Acceptance — checkable by playing |

| F22 | M5 | The field never holds more enemies at once than the authored wave names: overflow waits in the spawn queue and is never dropped, and nothing but the scheduler creates an enemy. | Push a large wave through one narrow line: every enemy the wave list names eventually appears, none is missing when the wave ends, and the on-field count never exceeds the authored concurrency. |

| F23 | M1 | One phase owner drives the six-phase state machine: LOBBY/READY → PREP/BUILD → COMBAT → INTERMISSION → (PREP/BUILD ∣ BOSS) → VICTORY ∣ DEFEAT. No surface advances state on its own timer, and no transition happens without its named event. | Watch the phase readout through a whole stage: it never skips, never re-enters a phase out of order, and every panel changes with it and not before. |

| F24 | M5 | A wave's spawn queue empties before the next wave is considered, and the next wave begins only when the queue is empty and no enemy remains alive. | Pull the last enemy of a wave out of reach of every tower: no new wave appears while it lives; kill it and the intermission begins. |

| F25 | M5 | Wave contents and entry order are authored per stage (Content of record); enemies enter from the field's authored approach directions, weighted toward the recorded distribution. | Clear the same stage twice with the same seed: the same waves arrive in the same order from the same sides. |

| F26 | M5 | Damage is computed from authored tables plus the player's enhancement and rank levels, and delivered as one discrete application event with its result; the computation lives in the platform-free core, not in a control. | Same seeded scenario replayed twice: the same kills in the same order. Numbers match the core's own arithmetic where that is runnable. |

| F27 | M5 | Status effects — burn, slow, stun, poison, invisibility-until-range, resistance — are applied as data with durations authored in seconds (Content of record), expire on their own event, and never carry information a paused game hides. | Slow one enemy with a Cryo Ray and one with Time Slow; read both speeds after the effect ends — back to base, no permanent creep. |

| F28 | S2 | Boss stages: the boss arrives as the final wave's climax, flips phase at the recorded HP threshold with its recorded phase behaviour, and a boss threat readout exists only while the boss is live. | Stage 3 at about 50% boss HP: the boss's behaviour visibly changes and its escort arrives; in Stage 1 no such readout ever appears. |

| F29 | M1 | Victory = every authored wave cleared with the Command Base alive; defeat = the Command Base destroyed. Both routes land on the results surface, and nothing else ends a stage. | Clear Stage 5 → VICTORY; feed the base → DEFEAT; no other path exits a run. |

| F30 | S2 | The five-stage campaign of Content of record is the whole v1 content set, and a stage's own unlock condition is enforced at the hub before entry. | Try to open Stage 4 without clearing Stage 3: blocked, with the reason shown as a keyed string. |
Talents and items.
| # | [S] | Requirement | Acceptance — checkable by playing |

| F31 | S5 | Six active talents (Content of record) at their recorded cost, cooldown and duration; usable only while a run is live; cooldown counted as data, so it survives any presentation being absent. | Fire Meteor twice back to back: refused while cooling, with the remaining time readable even with motion off. |

| F32 | S5 | Eight items (Content of record) with the recorded weighted drop table by enemy tier; Mora pouches credit the ledger on pickup; timed buffs act as data multipliers with a recorded duration. | Kill enough enemies to see a pouch drop and the balance move by the recorded amount; a buff's effect ends on schedule. |

| F33 | S5 | Talent unlock state persists (F36); a locked talent is shown as locked, never silently hidden or falsely offered. | Unlock a talent, leave, return: still unlocked, and a locked one reads as locked rather than missing. |
Progression, results and persistence.
| # | [S] | Requirement | Acceptance — checkable by playing |

| F34 | S1 | The hub presents the campaign as a readable route: five stages, their cleared state, their earned rating, and what is still locked. | From the hub, a second player can say which stages are done and which is next without being told. |

| F35 | S6 | Rank: a per-run veterancy track earned from kill EXP at the recorded thresholds (Content of record), costing no Mora, granting the recorded multiplicative bonuses, and resetting when a new stage begins. | Long Stage 5 run: rank rises on its own, the bonuses show in damage, and Stage 1 next visit starts at the bottom rank again. |

| F36 | M4 | The persisted set is exactly: cleared stages, per-stage rating, achievement flags, talent unlocks — one registry, versioned keys, sized against A5's confirmed count when it lands (NFR16). Nothing in-stage is persisted. | Clear stages, unlock a talent, earn an achievement; close and reopen the map: all four read back, and the starting Mora of a fresh run is unaffected. |

| F37 | M4 | The seven achievements (Content of record) are evaluated on their named events, each paying its recorded Mora once and setting its own persisted flag. | Trigger the first-victory achievement: paid once, flagged once, and not paid again on the next win. |

| F38 | M4 | Read-back is allowed to fail and must degrade honestly: where persistence is unavailable or unwritable, the run starts at the campaign's first stage, the session keeps playing, and no requirement above becomes unsatisfiable. | Simulate the no-persistence path in the editor: a full Stage 1-to-2 run remains playable and the results surface still reports what happened. |

| F39 | M1 | Leaving mid-stage, forfeiting, or exiting is a clean abandonment: the in-stage ledger, placed structures and rank are discarded, and no progress flag is set that the player did not earn. | Abandon Stage 3 mid-combat: hub still shows Stage 3 uncleared, balance untouched by the visit. |
Presentation, strings and legibility.
| # | [S] | Requirement | Acceptance — checkable by playing |

| F40 | all | Every player-visible string — including refusal reasons, phase names, structure and talent names, cost readouts, results text — is resolved from one key set with an authored EN and an authored CN entry created in the same change (NFR1, NFR2). | Switch locale and play the same route: no raw key, no missing slot, no one-sided string in either language. |
### 6.2 Surfaces

One surface is one screen family the player can be asked to use; a surface is not a module, a folder or a control inventory — no layout is implied here. Each row's waits-on column records which platform fact or open question it depends on, and decides none of them.

## 8. Phasing, exit criteria and the split-map fallback
### 8.1 Phasing

- Phase 0 — a short investigation. It settles the open questions and builds almost nothing. Measure the open platform questions in writing (one research issue each), run the test procedures in `docs/project/building/phase0-protocols/`, record every measured figure together with the work pass that measured it, and choose one of two routes: a single map, or the split-map fallback. Close the open decisions (D1, D2, D7) to the extent a human will; the platform-free core (the economy code, the tables, the wave scheduler and the random-number generator) is organised and exercised during Phase 0.

- Phase 1 — build the surfaces in parallel. One surface per owner, no two owners touching the same files, and nothing published in this phase — a half-built hub is not a map. Order does not matter; the wiring (M1-M7) is integrated last, and the integration owner is responsible for those wiring rows.
- Phase 2 — integrate, and publish once. Publication is one event, allowed only when the whole set passes (8.2); the publishing checklist is handed to the human, who alone publishes.
### 8.2 Whole-set exit criteria
The set a human reads before consenting to publication. Every row is pass/fail by playing; no row may be marked passed on the strength of an agent's own mockup.
1. Every 6.2 surface row passes its acceptance check and its NFR12 gate on the real map, in both locales.
2. Every 6.3 wiring row passes: one ledger (M2), one phase owner (M1), one persisted key registry (M4).
3. Every F-row's acceptance has been walked by a person who did not write it, in order, S1 to S6.
4. NFR1-NFR18 hold, or name their exception in writing; NFR12's gate has a dated human verdict beside it.

5. The platform questions of 5.2 are measured, each resolving into an ADR where the answer changes architecture — an unanswered question that a row depends on is a blocked publication, not a risk note.
6. Both locale key sets are identical, verified by opening both files, and the count is stamped at its home (`docs/project/building/ref-locale-denominator.md`).
7. D1, D2 and D7 are decided; where D2 is still open, no final gameplay sprite-data set claim may be made and the set fails.
8. A playtest path exists for all five stages end to end, silent and motion-off (NFR13, NFR14).
9. No row in this file cites an unconfirmed platform figure as its basis (R1, NFR17).
10. The creator-facing policy reading has happened by a human, and its name, version and date are recorded.
### 8.3 The split-map fallback — designed for from the start

If A7 answers that a script may not show and hide whole control groups, or if A5's confirmed count cannot hold S1-S6 at once, each surface becomes its own map with S1 as the entry point. Planned from the start, not used as a last resort:

- The economy stays in-run either way: Mora is session-scoped (F21), so the split never splits the balance; what the split threatens is read-back, and A8 decides whether one persisted key set survives across maps. If A8 answers per map, the progression data families (F36) must be given a new place or the campaign restructured — a scope change decided by a human, never absorbed silently.

- Cost named in advance: the phase driver (M1), ledger seam (M2) and the locale lookup (M7) are duplicated per map, and every hand-off between maps becomes an authored entry point rather than a show/hide.
- The exit criterion that changes: 8.2 row 1 is then checked per map, and row 5's A5/A7/A8 answers are the evidence attached to the decision.

# platform 鈥?measured platform behavior: row index and landing file

> A pre-2026-10-17 citation to `ref-measurements.md:<line>` must be resolved through the bridge table below.

Scope: the entry point to every measured platform row in this repo. New rows land in this file; the rows measured before 2026-10-17 are grouped by concern in the chunks listed below, because this file's body has a 250-line cap and past that a chunk splits by concern (`docs/project/index.md`). Each fact appears in exactly one chunk.

The consolidation decision is `docs/adr/ADR-0006-engine-md-lives-in-the-template.md`: measured platform behavior is recorded in exactly one place, in this template, a repo may measure but never keeps a second copy of a measured number, and every sister repository's `ENGINE.md` is a pointer here. The row convention is `docs/project/platform/law-adding-a-measurement.md`. A row is one build, one account, one day; it is not a budget to design against, and a dev-bench finding never closes a device question.

## The concern chunks

Each chunk opens with a scope line and keeps its rows under the heading of the repo that measured them. A chunk's row count is the count on the date its line states; a later row moves the count, not the earlier date. Counts below are as of 2026-10-22.

- `ref-measurements-client-ui.md` 鈥?control creation and templates, hierarchy, transforms, colour and alpha, tween and fill, layout, the payload-to-screen surface, and the editor's control counts. 77 rows, dated 2026-09-25 to 2026-10-20.

- `ref-measurements-performance.md` 鈥?the tick and its budget: per-tick cost, creation and write throughput, pacing, full-frame repaint, and the logging time base, plus the 2026-10-20 host sweep over the v2 build dials. 34 rows, dated 2026-09-25 to 2026-10-20.
- `ref-measurements-sessions.md` 鈥?playtest, editor and session mechanics, map and save lifecycle, stage flags, log capture. 21 rows, dated 2026-09-25 to 2026-10-07.
- `ref-measurements-dev-bench.md` 鈥?host, simulator and converter findings, including the 332 B/op memory anchor, the encoder and format benchmarks, the 32-bit bench-VM integer wrap and the bit window it destroys, the pricing/collection and RSS rows measured in another repo's product, the `source_layering` coat-ablation prune, the mid-grid candidates, the v2 `--bg-chain` window row, the 96x54 rescue sweep that found the first grid passing both bars on all three windows, and the tombstone that closes the build-grid downscale sweep. 78 rows, dated 2026-09-25 to 2026-10-22 (counted 2026-10-22: 16 rows under Genshin-IPC, 53 under miliastra-game-template, 9 under Vanguard-Arena). **Every row here is a host-side or simulator finding; none closes a device question.**

# project — the project documentation index

Always read this index on entering `docs/project/`. It is the routing table for this repo; there is no other index beside it.

## Routing

| Kind of thing | Home |
| --- | --- |
| A measured platform fact | one row in `../miliastra-game-template/docs/project/platform/ref-measurements.md` |
| How to build | `docs/project/building/` |
| A rule that is still true | `docs/specs/` |
| Operating the editor or the game | `docs/project/sessions/` |
| A rule for working on this repo | `docs/guides/` |
| A product or content decision | `docs/adr/` |
| In-flight work | `docs/plans/<date>-<topic>/` until it is settled and moved to its permanent home |
| A raw record | `archive/` — written once, never required reading |

## Naming and size

Three prefixes, on files and on index lines. `law-` is binding: read it before doing the kind of work the filename names. `ref-` is reference: open it only when the task touches the named topic, and it is the default for project knowledge. `work-` is in-flight notes for one effort: no `law-` or `ref-` file ever cites it, and it is settled into a permanent file or moved to `archive/` when the effort ends. This file is where these conventions are stated.

Each document covers one topic, stands alone, and opens with one scope line naming its section. Its body is capped at 150 lines; past that it splits by topic, never by part number, and the split updates this index in the same change. Each fact has exactly one home; other documents link to it instead of repeating it. English and its Chinese counterpart stay inside the same topic document.

## This directory

- `ref-glossary.md` — pointer to the glossary and path index at `CONTEXT.md`. Open when a task needs a term's definition, the Avoid list, or the path index.
- `ref-official-docs.md` — pointer to the mirrored official corpus. Open when a task needs the mirrored official 千星奇域 corpus.

## Sections

- `platform/index.md` — measured platform behavior and this repo's open platform questions. Open when a task needs a measured platform number or an open platform question.
- `building/index.md` — how this game is built. Open when a task reads or changes the build of the game.
- `sessions/index.md` — operating the editor and the game. Open when a task drives the editor or the game.
- `docs/guides/index.md` — procedures for working on this repo. Read before the kind of work a guide names.

1: # Read before writing an ADR — the `docs/adr/` convention
2: 
3: Short prose records of hard decisions: one decision, one file, flat — no topic folders. ADRs record
4: product and content decisions (what the game does, how it behaves, what ships); workplace and process
5: rules are never ADRs — they live in the `read-before-*.md` file that owns that kind of work, or in `AGENTS.md`. The live list is
6: `docs/adr/index.md`, one line per decision.
7: 
8: ## Layout
9: 
10: ```
11: docs/adr/
12:   index.md                       the live list
13:   law-writing-an-adr.md          this file — the convention (docs/guides/)
14:   ADR-0001-….md … ADR-00NN-….md  one decision per file
15: ```
16: 
17: The index is maintained by hand — there is no generator: adding a decision means adding its `index.md`
18: row in the same change, and if hand maintenance starts to hurt that is a ruling for `AGENTS.md`, never
19: a generator.
20: 
21: ## File anatomy
22: 
23: ```markdown
24: # ADR-0001 — <the decision, stated as a title>
25: 
26: Status: **Accepted** (YYYY-MM-DD — <the human ruling or issue that produced it>)
27: Topic: <1–2 lowercase tags>
28: Law: One sentence stating the decision.
29: 
30: ## Context
31: 
32: ## Decision
33: 
34: ## Consequences
35: ```

lines.text: # Read before writing an ADR — the `docs/adr/` convention
Short prose records of hard decisions: one decision, one file, flat — no topic folders. ADRs record
product and content decisions (what the game does, how it behaves, what ships); workplace and process
rules are never ADRs — they live in the `read-before-*.md` file that owns that kind of work, or in `AGENTS.md`. The live list is
`docs/adr/index.md`, one line per decision.
## Layout
docs/adr/
index.md                       the live list
law-writing-an-adr.md          this file — the convention (docs/guides/)
ADR-0001-….md … ADR-00NN-….md  one decision per file
The index is maintained by hand — there is no generator: adding a decision means adding its `index.md`
row in the same change, and if hand maintenance starts to hurt that is a ruling for `AGENTS.md`, never
a generator.
## File anatomy
```markdown
# ADR-0001 — <the decision, stated as a title>
Status: **Accepted** (YYYY-MM-DD — <the human ruling or issue that produced it>)
Topic: <1–2 lowercase tags>
Law: One sentence stating the decision.
## Context
## Decision
## Consequences
| Field | Required | Notes |
| `Status` | yes | `**Accepted** (date — what produced it)`; may wrap onto following lines; retired records get the ARCHIVED banner instead |
| `Topic` | yes | 1–2 lowercase tags (`platform`, `layout`, `art`, `localization`, `save`, `rules`, `economy`, `content`) |
| `Law` | yes | one sentence; this is the line that appears in `index.md` |
| `Supersedes` / `Superseded-by` | no | `ADR-00XX (what was superseded)` — used when only part of a record is replaced |
`Topic:`, `Law:` and `Superseded-by:` go after the whole status value, never inside it. The
`index.md` cell copies the record's `Law:` line word for word, plus the one plain cross-reference when
the record carries a `Supersedes`/`Superseded-by` line. A changed decision is
edited into its record, and the row is rewritten to that record's current `Law:` in the same change —
never a dated qualifier, never a silent rewrite.
## Rules
1. One decision per file — two decisions means two files.
2. IDs are permanent: global, sequential, four digits from `ADR-0001`, never reused or renumbered.
3. A record states the decision in force: a changed decision is edited in place, and only a
genuinely separate decision is a new ADR carrying `Supersedes: ADR-00XX`. Amendment blocks and
dated changelog entries are never used.
4. ADR before the code — a major architectural decision is recorded before the change goes in.
5. Short: one to two pages; longer means it is really two decisions.
6. Derive the next number by listing `docs/adr/`, never from memory.
7. Name the measurement you are waiting on: a `Law:` that assumes a confirmed figure (a cap, a tick rate,
a budget) is a defect — write what is unmeasured into the record and name the test that will settle it.
8. Cite, do not remember: every factual claim carries a reference relative to the repo root — path and section —
opened at the time of writing.
## Number allocation
This file is the home of planned ADR numbers. An ADR takes its number when its file is created — the file on
disk sets the number, and every planned entry is a suggestion only. A document that expects a future record says which
candidate number it is and points here (placeholder `ADR-00NN`); a planned number gives way without complaint to a record
already on disk, and after filing you re-point every planned number and name the change in the handover.
Permission to start work that an ADR already decided is a ticket question, not a record.
## Adding a decision
1. List `docs/adr/` and take the highest existing number + 1.
2. Create `docs/adr/ADR-00NN-<kebab-slug>.md` from the anatomy above.
3. Add its row to `docs/adr/index.md` in the same change — an ADR with no row in the index is not on record.
4. Name it after the issue or plan that motivated it.
## Superseding and retiring
Supersession is for a separate decision that replaces an older one: add the new ADR with
`Supersedes: ADR-00XX` and `Superseded-by: ADR-00ZZ` on the old one, then archive the old record in
place, with this notice as its very first line: `> **ARCHIVED (YYYY-MM-DD):** superseded by docs/adr/ADR-00ZZ-….md;
kept as historical reference.`
A change to a decision already in force is an edit in place of its own record — no new ADR, nothing
appended, no notice, because the ruling is still that record's own. A record whose rules moved out to a
