===== AGENTS.md
   1: # AGENTS.md — Taskworld Project · Sandbox-City
   3: How to behave in this repo. Product truth is `PRD.md`. Words and the path index are `docs/project/ref-glossary.md`. Decisions are `docs/adr/`. Conventions for `docs/project/` — prefixes, document size, one fact one home — are `docs/project/index.md`.
  13: Sandbox-City (Taskworld Project) re-expresses the Flash tower-defense Enigmata: Stellar War as a 千星奇域 map — free placement of defensive structures, timed enemy waves, boss stages, one Mora ledger — driven by Lua client scripts over editor-authored client controls. EN Taskworld Project, CN Sandbox-City; `Taskworld-Project` is the repo name only. Surfaces S1–S6 and wiring M1–M7 are registered in `PRD.md`. The shipping target is everything; a map per surface is designed from the start.
  15: The source set `other games reference material/enigmata-stellar-war/` is read-only and not a compatibility target. Mechanics and content are re-typed in Lua. No file of code, audio, font or string carries over. Gameplay sprites are code-owned data rendered through client controls (`docs/adr/ADR-0005-code-owned-gameplay-sprites.md`). Cover imagery is outside gameplay.
  19: Genshin Impact 千星奇域 UGC; the editor is 千星沙箱, PC-only (`PRD.md` § Platform constraints). No engine, package manager, test harness, filesystem, or build step in what ships. Payload scripts `require` only and read and write no file; persistence is cloud-save variables only.
  23: `platform-free-core/` is the one carve-out (`docs/adr/ADR-0002-platform-free-core-and-carve-out.md`): pure Lua naming no platform call, run under this machine's `lua.exe` as a development tool, never a payload dependency. Module law: `platform-free-core/README.md`. The 5.1-safe subset is policed by `dev/lua-gate/`, not by that interpreter — local Lua 5.4.5 parses what the subset bans (`docs/project/building/ref-lua-subset-gate.md`). A local named exactly `oddx` miscompiles; rename and re-run before believing the failure. A green local run is arithmetic evidence only, never proof the payload loads.
  30: - Settlement is event-driven. Mora changes on the settle event, never on a clock. Exactly one write seam (`PRD.md` F13, M2).
  32: - Fragile areas — report, do not fix. A change names the invariant: the Mora ledger write (never negative, re-granted at stage start, forfeit on leave) and its save-key namespace; the phase owner (`PRD.md` M1); the structure, enemy, enhancement and stage tables in `PRD.md` § Content of record; the placement-capacity rule (`PRD.md` F4) — eight placed structures including the Command Base.
  36: EN and CN are co-equal, authored together. No player-facing literal in code or in an editor text field. Both entries of a key land in the same change. Parity is opening `locale/en.lua` and `locale/zh_cn.lua`. Never import the source game's locale files. Do not quote a remembered key total.
  40: The legibility gate (`PRD.md` NFR12) is a human judgement. An agent cannot pass it. Capture is a pre-check, never acceptance. Where you cannot play, say the requirement is unverified. Graceful degradation is `PRD.md` NFR18; the game plays with motion off (NFR13).
  44: File a defect with a failing check under `issue-tracker/open/` before the fix. Do not file a doc or process issue. Do not write a handover file. Numbering and moves: `docs/guides/law-editing-issue-files.md`. An issue file is never deleted.
  46: ADRs are product and content decisions, written before the decision is implemented. Workplace rules are not ADRs. Convention: `docs/guides/law-writing-an-adr.md`. The live list is `docs/adr/index.md`.
  62: Never kill the game process. Exit a playtest in-game: Esc, then 中断挑战, then 离开. Force-kill `YuanShen.exe` only when the game is frozen and that path does not work.
  66: From the Genshin main menu: Esc, scroll to the bottom, 我的奇域. Esc on an editor tab returns to the editor menu; Esc again toggles the left bar. The third button on that bar is the save-file manager. Turn logging on every time the editor opens, or the session writes no `.gia`: 千星沙箱 window, 窗口 → 日志, scroll 选择单位 to the bottom, tick 客户端脚本. Further click-paths are `docs/project/sessions/law-editor-sessions.md`, and only during a Sandbox session.
===== CONTEXT.md
   3: Glossary and path index. Rules live in `AGENTS.md`. Product truth is `PRD.md`. Decisions live in `docs/adr/`.
  12: - **Platform-free core** (可移植核心): the pure-Lua rules region in `platform-free-core/` — it names no client control, no save variable and no platform call. Module law: `platform-free-core/README.md`. Avoid: engine, framework, backend, library.

3: One line per decision. **Hand-maintained** — there is no generator, so adding an ADR means adding its

11: a record carries a `Superseded-by`/`Supersedes` line, the cell adds that one plain cross-reference —

14: | ID | Topic | Law |
15: | --- | --- | --- |
16: | ADR-0001 | art, platform | Gameplay sprites enter code as data and render through client controls; no external gameplay image upload/import path exists, and a cover image is outside gameplay. |
17: | ADR-0002 | art, platform | Host-side Image-to-Lua conversion may emit reviewed plain-Lua art data for a consumer, but no shipped Miliastra payload may contain an image decoder, image file, filesystem reader, runtime loader, package-manager dependency, or external image-addressability route. |
18: | ADR-0003 | art, platform | The template carries three shared developer tools — the render kit (a platform-free, adapter-seamed Lua library under `platform-free-core/` with its dev harness under `dev/`), the image-to-lua compressor (`dev/image-to-lua/`), and a browser preview UI (`dev/preview-ui/`) — and none of them is product code: no gameplay art, no locale keys, no payload defaults ship from the template, every tool is optional to a product repo, and each tool versions independently of the template's own structure. |
19: | ADR-0004 | tooling, art | The template's developer tooling is built on a Python compressor (Pillow, NumPy, scikit-image, SciPy with its HiGHS solver, pyclipper; vtracer an optional extra) and a zero-build browser preview (vanilla ES modules over Canvas 2D, PixiJS the only sanctioned vendored upgrade), with GPL-licensed code and LGPL-bundled wheels excluded, no Pyodide, no Rust, no JS bundler, and zero node_modules files in the released tree. |
20: | ADR-0005 | content, tooling | Benchmark image fixtures MAY be committed to this repository by explicit addition through the SOURCES/checksums ritual, and committed fixtures must NOT be vendored into the published product repo. |
21: | ADR-0006 | platform, tooling | Measured platform behaviour lives in this template repository's docs/project/platform/ref-measurements.md — the consolidated union of every Miliastra repository's measurement rows, each row keeping its origin — and every other repository's ENGINE.md is a pointer to it: a repo may measure, but never keeps a second copy of a measured number. |
22: | ADR-0007 | tooling, rules | The compressor's approximation search is a plateau-stopped heuristic, never an exhaustive search: it terminates at the first verified non-improving candidate minimum — a content-based, deterministic rule, never wall-clock — toward the owner's expectation of roughly 10 seconds even for large high-resolution input, an expectation still unmet on the 256/512 classes and open on ISSUE-037. |
23: | ADR-0008 | tooling | Working resolution is an aspect-preserving max-dimension downscale dial — the filter is the `intake_resample` dial (NEAREST default, BOX the measured opt-in, ADR-0020), user-adjustable, default 128, identity when both sides are within the dial, applied to the whole image with no tiling — and one rule governs everywhere: the converter's `max_dimension` recipe key, imported (never copied) by every other consumer. |
24: | ADR-0009 | tooling, rules | A single-image run over 30 seconds in tests is terminated and drives an optimization obligation through deterministic depth levers — 30 seconds being a testing allowance only, with production targets of at most a few seconds per image worst case and real-time (~24 fps) for typical images on hardware worse than the dev machine's — and the budget lives only in the harness layer as wall-clock, never inside engine decisions. |
25: | ADR-0010 | tooling | The converter's palette handling is adaptive: source colours quantize at a default depth of 64 and merge down toward at most 16 by integer RGB similarity — merging only spatially neighbouring patches (or folding tiny specks), never non-similar or non-neighbouring ones — as a cheap pre-search converter pass, switched ON by default with every knob dial-able or switchable off (ADR-0015), and with in-search merge moves deferred. *(superseded by ADR-0015 for its opt-in landing shape and default-flip gate only)* |
26: | ADR-0011 | tooling, art | The engine's shape vocabulary — `rect`, `tri`, `rrect` — is kernel-faithful end-to-end: candidates are priced by the kernel's own rasterization rules, every committed op kind is paintable by every renderer mirror, and generation emits only kernel-valid candidates — one vocabulary, one set of rules, everywhere: engine, preview, harness. |
27: | ADR-0012 | tooling | The image→drawing browser UI keeps a single search kernel — the real Python engine imported in-process — and the browser only renders: it paints exactly the committed op sequence, in commit order, through the parity-checked renderer (raster.js); a JavaScript search port is rejected as a forking kernel. |
28: | ADR-0013 | art, tooling | Ring ops are suspended from all output deliverables (demo, previews) by construction — the ring vocabulary, its unmeasured 62% inner-radius rule and every switch that could emit a ring are deleted, the named refusals and the convention kernel's explicit-radii annulus primitive are retained for a rebuild from measured radii — and the suspension lifts only when the diagonal/rotated-shape fitter work passes the owner's 2×-bound 30° diagonal test and a visual re-evaluation follows. *(superseded by ADR-0011 for the whole record)* |
29: | ADR-0014 | tooling | The product approximation pipeline is greedy-only — no rate-distortion (λ) selection exists in any product path or product-facing default — and the dispatcher survives only as research tooling in `dev/approx-proto` with its frozen oracle, explicitly marked research-only, never shipped in a game. |
30: | ADR-0015 | tooling | The converter's colour pipeline is, by default, quantize-to-64 (the palette dial, dial-able to any value 1..256 through `palette.colors`) followed by the adaptive merge stage switched ON (source depth = the dial, target 16, threshold 900, speck fold on, every knob dial-able or switchable off through the existing recipe keys) — a separate stage that always runs between quantize and the shape approximation and never inside the search. |
31: | ADR-0016 | save, tooling | Op-list payloads save in a columnar format (ops split by kind, per-field columns, standard zigzag, x/y deltas, kind-RLE, per-column same-as-previous elision) whose default dialect is per-column static canonical Huffman with code lengths in the header, with LZ4-block as the `lz4-compat` dialect over the same packed stream and the fmtver-1 Lua text module as the `text` debug dialect. |
32: | ADR-0017 | art, tooling | One converter encodes two drawing-method recipes, chosen at encode time — anim is the DEFAULT (frame 0 ships as a full-program I-frame that instantiates a persistent client-control pool; later frames ship as P-frame mutation lists: exact matches persist at zero cost, near matches become at most 5 property-sets over x/y/w/h/colour, new content creates controls, stale content retires by HIDE) and static draw is OPT-IN, useful only when total game size is in strain (the whole frame ships and is drawn as one program per update — a drawing method, never a load-once lifecycle); the product axis is drawing method, never "offline vs in-game", because every payload decodes into the game as frames. |
33: | ADR-0018 | tooling | The greedy approximation path carries two owner-selectable, default-preserving dials — `budget_currency` (controls \| bytes \| frame), which denominates every rate term the greedy prices, and `lattice_k` (0 \| 1 \| 2), which quantizes generated rect and tri/ring integer coordinates to multiples of 2^k at generation — with defaults `controls` and `0` producing byte-identical output to the pre-dial engine, and the `bytes` table explicitly PROVISIONAL until the real per-kind costs of the payload format (ADR-0016) replace it. |
34: | ADR-0019 | tooling | The product greedy's per-program ceiling on experimental (tri/ring) commits is an owner-selectable, default-preserving dial — `max_experimental_ops` (mixed_ops keyword / CLI `--max-experimental-ops`, any positive int; one shared tri+ring budget, never per-kind; rrect cover ops never experimental and never capped by it) — with default 4 producing byte-identical output to the pre-dial engine, and a recorded-but-unapplied sweep recommendation of 8. |

85: | ADR-0073 | art, platform | A slot MAY carry a chain of adjacent ramps — the encoder keeps adjacent ramps, the default fitter emits them and the runtime hands off between them — but a native ramp pays only when it spans 4 or more frames, because one start costs 20.478 us against 6.72 us of frame time per write it replaces, and on the tracked busy fixture the fitter's ramps have a median span of 2 frames so the measured saving comes from HOLD rather than from ramps; wrapping one ramp in a `game.TweenSequence` remains a measured 5.78x loss and is not an optimization target. |

lines.text: # ADR index
One line per decision. **Hand-maintained** — there is no generator, so adding an ADR means adding its
row here. Convention: `docs/guides/law-writing-an-adr.md`.
The next number is derived by listing `docs/adr/`, never from this line.
Row grammar: the `Law` cell **mirrors that record's in-force `Law:` line verbatim** — never a summary,
no *Consequences* prose, no re-bolded clause (`docs/guides/law-writing-an-adr.md` § *File anatomy*).
A changed rule is edited in place in its record, so the cell always states what that ADR is now; where
a record carries a `Superseded-by`/`Supersedes` line, the cell adds that one plain cross-reference —
no dated qualifier, no amendment note.
| ID | Topic | Law |
| ADR-0001 | art, platform | Gameplay sprites enter code as data and render through client controls; no external gameplay image upload/import path exists, and a cover image is outside gameplay. |

| ADR-0002 | art, platform | Host-side Image-to-Lua conversion may emit reviewed plain-Lua art data for a consumer, but no shipped Miliastra payload may contain an image decoder, image file, filesystem reader, runtime loader, package-manager dependency, or external image-addressability route. |

| ADR-0003 | art, platform | The template carries three shared developer tools — the render kit (a platform-free, adapter-seamed Lua library under `platform-free-core/` with its dev harness under `dev/`), the image-to-lua compressor (`dev/image-to-lua/`), and a browser preview UI (`dev/preview-ui/`) — and none of them is product code: no gameplay art, no locale keys, no payload defaults ship from the template, every tool is optional to a product repo, and each tool versions independently of the template's own structure. |

| ADR-0004 | tooling, art | The template's developer tooling is built on a Python compressor (Pillow, NumPy, scikit-image, SciPy with its HiGHS solver, pyclipper; vtracer an optional extra) and a zero-build browser preview (vanilla ES modules over Canvas 2D, PixiJS the only sanctioned vendored upgrade), with GPL-licensed code and LGPL-bundled wheels excluded, no Pyodide, no Rust, no JS bundler, and zero node_modules files in the released tree. |

| ADR-0005 | content, tooling | Benchmark image fixtures MAY be committed to this repository by explicit addition through the SOURCES/checksums ritual, and committed fixtures must NOT be vendored into the published product repo. |

| ADR-0006 | platform, tooling | Measured platform behaviour lives in this template repository's docs/project/platform/ref-measurements.md — the consolidated union of every Miliastra repository's measurement rows, each row keeping its origin — and every other repository's ENGINE.md is a pointer to it: a repo may measure, but never keeps a second copy of a measured number. |

| ADR-0007 | tooling, rules | The compressor's approximation search is a plateau-stopped heuristic, never an exhaustive search: it terminates at the first verified non-improving candidate minimum — a content-based, deterministic rule, never wall-clock — toward the owner's expectation of roughly 10 seconds even for large high-resolution input, an expectation still unmet on the 256/512 classes and open on ISSUE-037. |

| ADR-0008 | tooling | Working resolution is an aspect-preserving max-dimension downscale dial — the filter is the `intake_resample` dial (NEAREST default, BOX the measured opt-in, ADR-0020), user-adjustable, default 128, identity when both sides are within the dial, applied to the whole image with no tiling — and one rule governs everywhere: the converter's `max_dimension` recipe key, imported (never copied) by every other consumer. |

| ADR-0009 | tooling, rules | A single-image run over 30 seconds in tests is terminated and drives an optimization obligation through deterministic depth levers — 30 seconds being a testing allowance only, with production targets of at most a few seconds per image worst case and real-time (~24 fps) for typical images on hardware worse than the dev machine's — and the budget lives only in the harness layer as wall-clock, never inside engine decisions. |

| ADR-0010 | tooling | The converter's palette handling is adaptive: source colours quantize at a default depth of 64 and merge down toward at most 16 by integer RGB similarity — merging only spatially neighbouring patches (or folding tiny specks), never non-similar or non-neighbouring ones — as a cheap pre-search converter pass, switched ON by default with every knob dial-able or switchable off (ADR-0015), and with in-search merge moves deferred. *(superseded by ADR-0015 for its opt-in landing shape and default-flip gate only)* |

| ADR-0011 | tooling, art | The engine's shape vocabulary — `rect`, `tri`, `rrect` — is kernel-faithful end-to-end: candidates are priced by the kernel's own rasterization rules, every committed op kind is paintable by every renderer mirror, and generation emits only kernel-valid candidates — one vocabulary, one set of rules, everywhere: engine, preview, harness. |

| ADR-0012 | tooling | The image→drawing browser UI keeps a single search kernel — the real Python engine imported in-process — and the browser only renders: it paints exactly the committed op sequence, in commit order, through the parity-checked renderer (raster.js); a JavaScript search port is rejected as a forking kernel. |

| ADR-0013 | art, tooling | Ring ops are suspended from all output deliverables (demo, previews) by construction — the ring vocabulary, its unmeasured 62% inner-radius rule and every switch that could emit a ring are deleted, the named refusals and the convention kernel's explicit-radii annulus primitive are retained for a rebuild from measured radii — and the suspension lifts only when the diagonal/rotated-shape fitter work passes the owner's 2×-bound 30° diagonal test and a visual re-evaluation follows. *(superseded by ADR-0011 for the whole record)* |

| ADR-0014 | tooling | The product approximation pipeline is greedy-only — no rate-distortion (λ) selection exists in any product path or product-facing default — and the dispatcher survives only as research tooling in `dev/approx-proto` with its frozen oracle, explicitly marked research-only, never shipped in a game. |

| ADR-0015 | tooling | The converter's colour pipeline is, by default, quantize-to-64 (the palette dial, dial-able to any value 1..256 through `palette.colors`) followed by the adaptive merge stage switched ON (source depth = the dial, target 16, threshold 900, speck fold on, every knob dial-able or switchable off through the existing recipe keys) — a separate stage that always runs between quantize and the shape approximation and never inside the search. |

| ADR-0016 | save, tooling | Op-list payloads save in a columnar format (ops split by kind, per-field columns, standard zigzag, x/y deltas, kind-RLE, per-column same-as-previous elision) whose default dialect is per-column static canonical Huffman with code lengths in the header, with LZ4-block as the `lz4-compat` dialect over the same packed stream and the fmtver-1 Lua text module as the `text` debug dialect. |

| ADR-0017 | art, tooling | One converter encodes two drawing-method recipes, chosen at encode time — anim is the DEFAULT (frame 0 ships as a full-program I-frame that instantiates a persistent client-control pool; later frames ship as P-frame mutation lists: exact matches persist at zero cost, near matches become at most 5 property-sets over x/y/w/h/colour, new content creates controls, stale content retires by HIDE) and static draw is OPT-IN, useful only when total game size is in strain (the whole frame ships and is drawn as one program per update — a drawing method, never a load-once lifecycle); the product axis is drawing method, never "offline vs in-game", because every payload decodes into the game as frames. |

| ADR-0018 | tooling | The greedy approximation path carries two owner-selectable, default-preserving dials — `budget_currency` (controls \| bytes \| frame), which denominates every rate term the greedy prices, and `lattice_k` (0 \| 1 \| 2), which quantizes generated rect and tri/ring integer coordinates to multiples of 2^k at generation — with defaults `controls` and `0` producing byte-identical output to the pre-dial engine, and the `bytes` table explicitly PROVISIONAL until the real per-kind costs of the payload format (ADR-0016) replace it. |

| ADR-0019 | tooling | The product greedy's per-program ceiling on experimental (tri/ring) commits is an owner-selectable, default-preserving dial — `max_experimental_ops` (mixed_ops keyword / CLI `--max-experimental-ops`, any positive int; one shared tri+ring budget, never per-kind; rrect cover ops never experimental and never capped by it) — with default 4 producing byte-identical output to the pre-dial engine, and a recorded-but-unapplied sweep recommendation of 8. |

| ADR-0020 | tooling | The working-resolution downscale's interpolation is a dial — `intake_resample`, NEAREST by default (ADR-0008's law stands, byte-identical output) with BOX as the measured opt-in area average (~9–12% fewer ops at unchanged tri adoption on robin) — recorded by absence at the default, owned by the converter's recipe key, and carried into the engine's image front door through that one import, never a second resize rule. |

| ADR-0021 | art, tooling | The anim pipeline carries two INDEPENDENT hard ceilings — a stock ceiling `caps_max_controls` bounding live+hidden pooled controls, and flow ceilings `caps_max_creates_per_frame` and `caps_max_mutations_per_frame` (a blunt proxy counting property-sets + retires) — never a combined weighted budget, which would re-introduce the scrapped-λ hidden exchange rate (ADR-0014) and is deferred until a device probe measures per-action costs; enforcement is same-kind slot recycling followed, in order, by create-deferral (debt carried into later frames, round-trip equality once paid) and frame splitting (two half-rate sub-frames at t and t+half), with honest smallest-impact drops after the ladder and static (all-creates) programs failing loudly with dial guidance instead of degrading; runtime hitch defence is a dt-paced content-time clock with CLOCK-SKIP — at most one present per tick, overdue frames skipped, never a queued catch-up burst — plus rolling dt/FPS telemetry, because a static cap cannot DETECT tick overrun; and every dial is default-off and byte-preserving: with all caps unset, emitted payloads and call streams are byte-identical to the uncapped pipeline. |

| ADR-0022 | save, tooling | Sequences of frame payloads (clips) may save in a `clip-stream` container — the frame bodies of one per-clip frame dialect (frame-dialect byte `H`, `P`, `K` or `D` — `H`/`P` are standalone payloads chosen per measured size at encode time, while `K` (columnar-book) and `D` (delta-pframes) are not standalone-decodable and are emitted only by their own opt-in builders) carried as segments of raw-DEFLATE (RFC 1951, zlib `wbits=-15`, pinned level 9) with a segment table (frame count and byte length per segment; segment-atomic decode, budgeted stepping), decoded on device by this repo's ORIGINAL inflate written from the public RFC — never a port of third-party decoder code — and chosen INSTEAD of per-frame columnar payloads only for multi-frame clips/animations (a single static image keeps the per-frame dialects of ADR-0016); repeated-shape dedup rides the stream's LZ back-references and NO separate instancing machinery will be built. |

| ADR-0023 | art, tooling | The clip payload's frame-record grammar gains two opt-in, default-off, byte-preserving compression record modes — the implicit base-color frame (when a frame's painting is majority one colour, the record carries that base colour once and emits ONLY non-base ops; painting treats unpainted cells as the base for that frame, the reference's mode-1 idiom) and the hold-frame token (a 1-byte "repeat last frame" record for identical consecutive frames whose runtime apply is a no-op) — with the encoder declining (emitting the ordinary record) whenever the mode does not verify or does not save bytes; with both dials off, every emitted stream is byte-identical to the pre-extension pipeline, pinned against the committed fixtures. |

| ADR-0024 | save, platform | Every Lua file on the shipping surface (`platform-free-core/**/*.lua`, payload_format.lua primarily) is written to the Lua 5.3 grammar and stdlib only — no 5.4-only construct (`<const>`/`<close>` attributes, `warn`, `coroutine.close`, 5.4 lexical scoping) may ride into the device player — while the dev-side interpreters and gates stay on the local Lua 5.4 (a strict superset for this codebase), so both versions run the same self-checks green. |

| ADR-0025 | art, tooling | The anim P-frame grammar gains two opt-in, default-off, byte-preserving whole-frame transform records — the camera-pan `pan(dx, dy, covered)` (one record instead of the N position property-sets of every conforming matched control) and the palette-permutation `permute(table)` (one moved-entries table instead of N colour-sets) — detected at encode time by threshold-gated pattern recognition over the native diff stream, verified per frame against the frame program with the engine's own composite, and a RUNTIME HONESTY LAW: absent the ISSUE-009 probe 11 container-parenting result, the runtime applies both records by LOOP — N property-sets, not one — so every byte/churn saving is reported alongside the unchanged (or honestly worse) expanded runtime call count, and the flow-cap accounting (ADR-0021) counts EXPANDED sets, never record count. |

| ADR-0026 | tooling | The greedy carries an opt-in, default-off, byte-preserving polygon pass — `polygon_pass` (mixed_ops keyword / CLI `--polygon-pass`) that claims each same-colour connected component (no holes, ≥16 cells, every ear within the 0.75 px isoceles-model tolerance, inside the kernel's tri domain) as FIRST-CLASS tri ops fitted by the engine's one fitting law `fit_tri_op` in the render path's own convention (unrotated-origin `(x, y)`, SetLocalRotation `deg`), structural like rrect cover ops — never experimental, never drawing on `max_experimental_ops` — and the default path stays byte-identical. *(superseded by ADR-0030 for the pass-local fitting clause only)* |

| ADR-0027 | tooling | The product greedy carries an opt-in wall-time stop — `time_budget` (mixed_ops keyword / CLI `--time-budget SECONDS`, any positive finite float; default None = unbounded, no clock read, byte-identical) — checked at mixed_ops entry's clock start, at round entry, before each candidate's pricing, and per residual component in the final exact cover (a deadline stop COMPLETES the program with the exact bands cover — ADR-0028; always a complete valid renderable program, never a fallback encoder), with capped runs being non-deterministic TIMED SAMPLES to which digest gates do not apply, and the dispatcher refusing the dial (ADR-0019 convention). *(superseded by ADR-0028 for the stop-behaviour clause only)* |

| ADR-0028 | tooling | On any `time_budget` deadline stop — scoring stage or mid-cover — the program is COMPLETED with the engine's existing exact bands machinery (`runs_bands` / vertical band merge over the residual components the stop reached, `cover_cells` at `allow_rrect=False` in `_covers_for_residuals`, no clock read past the stop), so a stopped program is always a complete, valid image — op-heavy and disclosed via `cover_source` in {"min-rect", "cheap-exact", "mixed"} plus `complete_s` in the `time_budget` report block — with the dial unset staying byte-identical. |

| ADR-0029 | tooling | fit_tri_op stores (x, y) as the UNROTATED box top-left — centre − (w/2, h/2) in screen axes with the apex pinned to the tip — per the render contract every consumer anchors (ideal_tri_mask offline, write_lua → the shared ISSUE-017 kernel → the device), a default-path bug fix with no dial: default digests move for every program that fitted displaced tris, and all standard baselines and the ADR-0019 dial-test pins are re-recorded, never silently. |

| ADR-0030 | tooling | The greedy's polygon pass — ADR-0026's same-colour first-class tri claims — runs only behind the explicit opt-in (`mixed_ops` kwarg `polygon_pass=True`; CLI `--polygon-pass`; the product encode default is ADR-0031's rect-only), auto-offs when `allow_tri=False`, never runs under `--dispatch`, and is fitted by the engine's one fitting law `fit_tri_op` (the pass-local `_polygon_fit_tri` is RETIRED); the dial-off run is byte-identical to the ADR-0029 post-fix engine (the four standard legs' pinned ops digests). *(superseded by ADR-0031 for the DEFAULT-ON clause only)* |

| ADR-0031 | tooling | A normal product encode emits RECT only — `mixed_ops` / `build_all` default `allow_tri=False`, `allow_rrect=False` and `polygon_pass=False`, and the CLI defaults `--no-allow-tri` / `--no-allow-rrect` with the polygon pass off unless `--polygon-pass` is stated — while tri, rrect and the polygon pass stay in the tree and emit again only when a caller turns the dial on explicitly. |

| ADR-0032 | tooling, platform | The render kit's create pacer defaults to unpaced — `rk_pacer.new` defaults `create_per_tick` to unlimited within a tick and `limiter_s` to 0 (no inter-batch hold), so a default pacer drains its whole create queue in the tick that opens the batch, its only default brake being the first refusal's latch (one log line, backlog dropped, growth frozen, surfaced through `census` and the meters) — while `create_per_tick >= 1` and `limiter_s > 0` remain exact opt-in dials for a caller that wants to pace, and destroy keeps its own paced default (`destroy_per_tick = 4`). |

| ADR-0033 | tooling | An explicit control-budget encode may search a finite deterministic ladder of the existing resolution, palette, and BOX intake choices to emit at most N axis-aligned rect controls on the original canvas, report its selected dimensions, palette, and premultiplied-RGBA quality, and fail before writing output when an explicit quality bound is unmet; the default encode is unchanged. |

| ADR-0034 | tooling | The frame prototype gains a default-off temporal_stable dial that reuses the prior ordered decomposition when bounded integer translation and consistent recoloring make the reused program paint what the target frame's own program paints, declines to ordinary encoding otherwise, and reports logical fields, expanded backend setters, visibility, creations and bytes separately without promising a group-write primitive. *(superseded by ADR-0061, the exactness acceptance clause only)* |

| ADR-0035 | tooling, art | The opt-in fast rectangle encoder rewrites the quantized image into fewer rectangles while trying neighbour merges and at most three background covers under a deterministic work cap; quadtree encoding uses it after approximation without changing legacy encoder defaults. |

| ADR-0036 | tooling, platform | Decode-ahead may adapt to supplied update headroom within explicit content-time, operation and estimated decoded-memory limits, and an opt-in RECT driver may prepare hidden back banks before a due-frame visibility sweep, while defaults retain one drawing pool and fixed decoding and no native group-flip or device speed is claimed. |

| ADR-0037 | tooling, art | The fast rectangle reducer may explicitly try column bands and four fixed local-region layouts after its legacy candidates under the same deterministic work cap, accepting only complete strict-count improvements whose program verifies against the input grid while omitted switches preserve existing artifacts and runtime behavior. *(superseded by ADR-0042 for the opt-in and omitted-switch clauses only)* |

| ADR-0038 | tooling, platform | An explicitly selected RECT I/P mount may replay the existing RGB event grammar with bounded sequential preparation and commit only the newest complete due state, while full-frame defaults remain unchanged and dependent events are never skipped with presentation. |

| ADR-0039 | tooling | The product converter exposes the engine's polygon pass as ONE opt-in recipe dial `shape_pass` — legal only with the `argmin` strategy, recorded only when `true`, default absent/false and byte-identical to the rect-only encode (ADR-0031's default stands) — driving TRI claims only while rrect and ring stay unexposed, and preview/convert emit validated tri ops while the SHIPPABLE-Lua gate (`check_shippable`) keeps refusing tri until the unmeasured on-device tri rendering probe passes (tri is `probe_status: "unprobed"` in `dev/image-to-lua/src/image_to_lua/vocabulary.py`; the browser kernel's raster.js and the payload dialect already round-trip tri). |

| ADR-0040 | tooling | Source-resolution RECT layering is the opt-in converter recipe dial `source_layering` — legal only with `encoding:"ops"` + `strategy:"fast"`, recorded only when true, default absent/false byte-identical — whose dial-on path analyses the pre-downscale source, layers big same-colour regions as bounding-rect first coats under a keep-only-if-better gate, repairs the remainder with the fast arm's own `reduce_rects`, replays with rect ops only, and falls back to the dial-off fast program whenever the layered program is not strictly shorter. |

| ADR-0041 | tooling, platform | The render kit carries two version values — a hand-set human-readable milestone label `RENDER_KIT_VERSION` (`"1.0.0"`, the release marker a person bumps per release) and a content-derived 16-hex-digit FNV-1a fingerprint `RENDER_KIT_STAMP` (computed by `dev/render-kit/build_mount.lua` over the 14 module bodies in mount order) — so a consumer logs a readable version while any byte-visible kit revision still changes a number by itself. |

| ADR-0042 | tooling, art | The fast reducer ALWAYS tries the column-band cover ("Try vertical drawing strips", recipe key `fast_columns`) and the fixed local-region backgrounds ("Try local background regions", recipe key `fast_regions`), and both dials are deleted from every surface — the preview-page checkboxes, the recipe keys and their allowlist, and the docs that enumerated them — so a `strategy:"fast"` encode has no off switch and its bytes move for recipes that previously omitted the switches. |

| ADR-0045 | tooling, art | The frame prototype gains a default-off, byte-preserving offline GOP encoder (`gop.py`) that chooses each frame's predictor over the WHOLE clip by a fixed per-edge cost proxy, emits the chosen structure in topological DECODE order (a stream may therefore be non-display-order and may use a FUTURE reference), and ships the ordinary I-frame-only stream whenever no structure beats it in bytes, with the decoded stream checked frame by frame against `paint(frames[t])` for every DISPLAY index `t` (engine composite), and `mode="off"` byte-identical to `payload.encode_full_stream`. |

| ADR-0056 | art, platform | The clip path's animation bank is DEFAULT-ON — the clip's DISTINCT frame contents (each canonicalised to the origin) built ONCE as hidden controls in ONE FLAT POOL (never nested subtrees), with a pool index recording which controls belong to which entry, then addressed per frame by an entry index plus an integer position offset — showing an entry costs one visibility write per control — with the decoded replay's paint checked against `paint(frames)` on every frame, with the encoder DECLINING (shipping the baseline payloads byte-identically) whenever the bank does not verify, every frame is already distinct, or the bank does not save bytes, so a default-on clip whose content does not repeat ships the dial-off artifact byte for byte; naming any other clip carriage, or a non-default `payload_dialect`, selects that instead, and `anim_bank: false` switches the bank off; there is NO CONTROL CEILING — the dial REPORTS the bank's size honestly and never asserts one — and the exposure this accepts is content that repeats a LARGE frame many times, where the bank wins bytes while the control count climbs. |

| ADR-0052 | save, tooling | Several clips in one game may share ONE raw-DEFLATE preset dictionary (RFC 1951 §3.2.3 / zlib `deflateSetDictionary` semantics) carried by an opt-in, default-off, byte-preserving clip container dialect byte `D` (the container slot ADR-0022's `C` occupies — distinct from the `D` clip frame-dialect byte) — the ≤ window−262 (32506 B) dictionary is preloaded into the LZ77 window of the repo's ORIGINAL pure-Lua inflate (`payload_format.M.inflate_raw(src, dict)`), so a segment's distance may reach before its own output start with no new entropy coder and no new frame grammar, a `dict_id` (FNV-1a 32-bit) stamp pins both sides to exactly the same dictionary, and the shipped `C` carriage is byte-identical when the dial is off. |

| ADR-0046 | tooling | The converter gains an OPT-IN, default-off, byte-preserving perceptual rate-allocation mode (`image_to_lua.perceptual`, dial `PerceptualConfig`) that re-weights a painter-ordered rect list by motion-discounted edge saliency and induced error and drops the low-importance ops, together with two explicitly-labelled APPROXIMATION scores — a GFM-like edge-similarity score (`gfm_like_score`, following GFM's sourced structure: odd-Gabor edge response, luminance/chrominance similarity, `SQ = SG^1·SC^0.04`, max-magnitude pooling) and a flat-region banding score (`banding_like_score`) — under the lane's correctness law: dial off returns the input op list unchanged (byte-identical baseline), a reduced program is checked to round-trip through the payload codec (`paint(decode(encode(reduced))) == paint(reduced)`), and any frame whose reduction does not strictly shrink the encoded bytes DECLINES to the ordinary program; the Gabor kernel parameters, the RGB→LMN matrix and the BBAND visibility formula are unpublished and are labelled approximations, so neither score is claimed as the exact GFM or BBAND, and the mode is reported as a measured NEGATIVE on the fixture (perceptual loses GFM-like score to uniform allocation at matched bytes). |

| ADR-0050 | art, tooling | The clip payload gains an opt-in, default-off, byte-preserving REGIONAL temporal-consolidation mode in two forms — Mode A, a per-region hold record over a fixed block grid in which a region whose rendered content is unchanged for K frames emits ONE record carrying `dur = K·dt` instead of K records, its decoded output checked against the grids every frame — and Mode B, a LOSSY near-duplicate merge driven by an explicitly declared palette-step tolerance, off by default, which records every suppressed change in a manifest and bounds the per-cell distortion it introduces — with the encoder declining (emitting the ordinary record) whenever a mode does not verify or does not save bytes, the whole-frame blanket hold form explicitly out of scope (that is ADR-0023's hold token, SHIPPED-OFF), and the observation that λ = ∞ (no approximation) degenerates the hold-length assignment to "emit exactly at change frames", so no DP is required for Mode A. |

| ADR-0054 | art, tooling | The product ANIM path gains one opt-in, default-off, byte-preserving native tween record — a frame range in which ONE control's tint (`imageColor`) or fill (`fillAmount`) changes along a documented easing curve is replaced by a single record (target, easing enum member, duration, loops) — detected at encode time by threshold-gated run recognition over consecutive frames, with the decoded artifact checked against `paint(frames)` every frame, and a RUNTIME HONESTY LAW ported from ADR-0025: the ENGINE's interpolation is what saves runtime work, our simulator proves only OUR curve math, so every byte/churn saving is reported alongside the EXPANDED property-set count (one set per replaced frame, which is what the ADR-0021 flow caps must count — EXPANDED sets, never record count) and the native tween-call count; the scope is TINT and FILL ONLY as a deliberate product choice — tint and fill tweening is device-measured (`docs/project/platform/ref-measurements-client-ui.md:61`) and transform tweening is device-measured too, existence and monotonicity only (`:76`), while curve fidelity and timing stay unmeasured for both — and the encoder DECLINES to the ordinary record whenever a record does not verify or does not save bytes. |

| ADR-0053 | art, tooling | The product op path gains an opt-in, default-off, byte-preserving alpha extension — a `blend ∈ {SOURCE, OVER}` notion on the op (derived from the palette entry's alpha, an explicit per-op `blend` key overriding it) plus a 64-entry RGBA palette of (colour, alpha) pairs, carried in a new `RKA` container whose base is the EXACT standalone product payload — where OVER is Porter-Duff source-over in exact integer arithmetic with round-half-up (`Co = (Cs·as + Cd·ad·(1−as)) / ao`, `ao = as + ad·(1−as)`), which on an opaque destination is bit-identical to the repo's pinned `raster.blend_rgb`; the decoded output is checked against `composite_over(ops)` and the decline rule (no OVER op, or an opaque tessellation that is no larger and fits the product palette, ships the ordinary product payload byte-identically) applies; with the dial off every emitted artifact is byte-identical to the pre-extension pipeline, and the platform's OVER *rendering* is recorded as NOT device-verified (only the alpha field's read/write is measured). |

| ADR-0048 | tooling, art | A frame may be encoded as a delta against the previous frame's painted grid — the changed-cell mask is computed, a legal rect cover of exactly those cells is derived by the converter's own row-run + band merge, and the derived rects ride an ordinary columnar payload that decodes by painting OVER the retained previous grid — the derived delta is checked against the frame program (`paint_over(prev, decode(encode(prev, ops)))` against `paint(ops)`) for every frame, with the encoder DECLINING (emitting the baseline full-frame payload byte-identically) whenever the derived delta does not verify, is not strictly smaller than the baseline, or needs MORE rects than the baseline frame list — ops are the measured bottleneck, so a byte saving never buys an op regression — and with the dial off the artifact is byte-identical to the baseline. |

| ADR-0055 | tooling, platform | A painter-ordered rect program may carry ONE opt-in `rotscale` op — a source rect drawn at whole integer degrees and optional integer non-uniform scale, emitted only when a pure-integer simulator matches the cell set of the upright-rect run it replaces and the carriage is strictly smaller than the baseline payload; the dial is default-off and byte-identical to the baseline artifact when off, and the simulator is our arithmetic model, never a claim about how the device renders a rotated control. |

| ADR-0047 | save, tooling | The product payload format gains an opt-in, default-off, byte-preserving frame dialect byte `F` (`fieldcode-adaptive`) that codes rect fields with a per-field adaptive binary range coder whose contexts come from neighbouring records and from the other dimension of the same record — x/y as previous-record deltas, w/h as direct adaptive value trees keyed by the other dimension, and the palette index keyed by the previous record's index — with the encoder declining to the shipped payload bytes whenever the frame carries a non-rect kind, exceeds the modelled dimension or magnitude bound, or the re-code is not strictly smaller, and the dialect reachable only through this module's own seam (`encode_fieldcode` / `decode_fieldcode`), because the shipped clip-stream carriage does not yet admit the `F` byte. |

| ADR-0049 | save, tooling | The rect payload gains two opt-in, default-off, byte-preserving clip modes — a clip-wide shape dictionary (each distinct `(w,h)` stored once, each rect emitting one shape index in place of the `w` and `h` columns) and neighbour-colour index prediction (a rect's palette index coded as BELOW / LEFT / NEITHER against the already-painted canvas, HEVC-SCC palette-mode style, with a literal only on NEITHER) — riding a `DCT1` clip container that also carries, per coded column, one canonical-Huffman alphabet chosen as the smaller of a clip-pooled alphabet and a per-frame alphabet, with the decoded clip checked against `paint(frames)` for every frame and mode, and the encoder declining (emitting the baseline per-frame columnar-huffman payloads) when a non-rect kind is present or the container does not beat the baseline total; flip/mirror bits are NOT implemented because axis-aligned rectangles are symmetric under both flips, so one stored shape already serves every orientation. |

| ADR-0057 | save, platform | A composed artifact's `cfg.payloads` entry is either a standalone payload STRING (dialects `H`/`P`/`L`/`F`) or a payload-less `{ ops, meta }` frame — the shape the shipped reader already returns for the `D` (delta-pframes) and `K` (columnar-book) clip frame dialects, which have no standalone payload by construction — and a payload-less entry is presented UNAMORTIZED: the driver draws it from the expanded ops list on its own dt clock, the core player's payload-string path is not constructed for that carriage, and `decode_ahead`/`prerender` are refused by name on it. |

| ADR-0058 | tooling, art | Encoder quality is reported at the target canvas scale by the offline perceptual metric and the preview UI, with device verification human-eye-gated — every carriage's round-trip gate verifies the committed program (`paint(decode(encode(program))) == paint(program)`), and encoder determinism (ADR-0009 byte-identity) stands unchanged. |

| ADR-0059 | art, platform | The client SFX asset namespace is not an instrument or melody bank — pitched music rides the server native-BGM channel, client-conducted (per-note `NA_BgmSet` speed, the `bgmx7` route the owner accepted and told us to continue) — while client `PlayAudio2D`/`StopAudio`/`IsAudioAlive` remains the ordinary sound-effect path (UI clicks, one-shots) and the client-SFX melody-banking effort is retired. |

| ADR-0060 | save, tooling | `payload_carriage` names two orthogonal axes — a TEXT EMBEDDING (`escaped`, the 4x `\NNN` default, or `base85`, a `b85_decode` call that materializes to the same bytes) and a clip CONTAINER (`clip-stream`, `clip-pframes`) — so `base85` is admitted beside the `clip_delta`, `anim_bank` and `clip_permute` carriages while the container values stay refused there as unproven container-on-container stacking, an absent key still composes the byte-identical escaped artifact, and no `payload_format`, driver or adapter change is needed because every reader sniffs the materialized string. |

| ADR-0061 | art, platform | A runtime update repaints a FROZEN control partition and changes tint only — never re-issuing geometry and never re-covering a frame — under a declared lossy tolerance (probe-grid mean SSIM floor 0.90, RMS 5.70, owned by the human owner and reported by the encoder per run), with repaint (all three setters every frame) and redraw (per-frame cover plus visibility churn) both refuted on device and no new runtime mechanism added, because `rk_diff` already prices `tint` at cost 1 and `driver.apply_row` already emits the RGBA setter alone when geometry is unchanged. *(supersedes ADR-0034 for its exactness acceptance clause only)* |

| ADR-0062 | save, platform | Carriage identity is resolved per frame, not per artifact — the encoder may choose `cell_delta`, fieldcode `F` or `H` independently for every frame, each frame's own record carries the identity the decoder reads, and no new writer may assume one carriage for a whole clip, while this record authorizes no dispatcher, container or shipped-format change. |

| ADR-0063 | art, save | v2 is an ADDITIVE, opt-in, versioned clip path in which one segment carries its geometry, paint order and slot ids ONCE in an anchor record and every slot then carries its own RGBA colour track as independent HOLD, STEP or LINEAR-ramp records — a ramp binds only when its fit reproduces the declared source-relative quality at every source sample and the packed event stream is smaller after start/stop cost, a refused or capped native tween falls back to STEP writes evaluated from the SAME encoded track (never a snap to one endpoint), the stream is chunked and decoded lazily with compact resident state, every record resolves its own mode identity without assuming any shipped carriage composes with the stream, and every v1 API, recipe default and artifact stays byte-identical. *(superseded by ADR-0072, the LINEAR-only clause; every other clause stands)* |

| ADR-0064 | art, save | `v2.fit.fit_track_optimal` — the exact HOLD/STEP/RAMP parse under L-infinity — is the default track fitter of the v2 clip path, selected when `fitter` is `None`, and `max_channel_error` stays 0, so the default build keeps the exact-colour quality bar and only changes which parse is emitted; `fitter="greedy"` remains the explicit opt-out and reproduces the pre-ISSUE-329 build byte for byte. |

| ADR-0065 | art, platform | An over-detailed source is built at a reduced BUILD RESOLUTION, never at a coarser cell — `--cell` is the adapter's display scaler, chosen so the reduced build fills the 600x338 window, `--cell-prepass` stays OFF by default and is not the product lever, and the shipped default build resolution holds until a real-content build measures the point; the grid is never chosen by shrinking the picture until the write ceiling stops complaining. *(superseded by ADR-0071, the clause that made the write budget the reason to pick a grid; every other clause stands)* |
| [ADR-0066 (Proposed)](ADR-0066-stored-only-carriage-on-the-product-path.md) | save, platform | The v2 product path ships `stored` chunks only and never `deflate`. |

| ADR-0067 | art, tooling | `max_channel_error` stays at its default 0 for a v2 build. Raising it to 2 is NOT a byte win on the per-slot colour-track pipeline, and the long-ramp probe that would make it one has not run on device. |

| ADR-0068 | art, tooling | The default `--floor` stays 0.95 and a floor is a PLANNER INPUT, not a quality guarantee — `quality.accepted` is the only statement about delivered quality, `--quantize` is a QUALITY CEILING that no cover can beat, and a product build meets 0.95 by choosing a grid for the picture it delivers or else lowers `--floor` and records the quality it accepts, never reads a bigger palette as the fix. *(superseded by ADR-0071, the clause that made the write budget the reason to pick a grid; every other clause stands)* |

| ADR-0069 | art, tooling | `max_concurrent` defaults to **256**, not 64, because at 64 the build refuses two of three measured windows for a cost of nothing — every ramp on the shippable setting is 2 frames long, so a refused start costs one extra write (+0.52% and +0.71% of those plans' writes) while the per-frame peak does not move at any cap from 31 to 4096. 256 is a number chosen so the build stops blocking, not a device-validated ceiling: it is unmeasured on device and a harder clip can exceed any fixed value. |

| ADR-0070 | art, tooling | `exact_band_cover` joins two same-colour runs only when they share the same `x` and `w`, because dropping `x` from the key (`dev/video-v2/v2/planner_candidates.py:161`) makes the cover inexact — measured on frame 412 it produced 8,471 non-uniform rectangles of 34,309, over-painted 18,781 cells and left 19,705 unpainted, and on frame 422, 11,759 of 41,884 — so the `x` in the key is a correctness requirement, not the fragmenting bug; the fragmentation is a property of the content (25,058 same-colour 4-connected components against 45,793 shipped rects, with greedy meshing within +1.7%), and the exact-cover route to fewer slots is a coarser build grid (ADR-0065), never a relaxed merge. |

| ADR-0071 | art, tooling | A build grid is never chosen by measuring the device's per-frame write ceiling and then shrinking the picture until it fits; the write budget stays at the shipped 4,341 figure, raising that figure is never a reason to coarsen a grid, and effort goes into making a frame need fewer writes, never into showing fewer cells. |

| ADR-0072 | art, platform | A v2 ramp carries its easing curve as a free per-ramp parameter whose default stays `Linear`, and no `Enum.EaseType` name is forbidden — a non-Linear curve may be emitted only once the fallback evaluator can reproduce that curve bit-exactly from the encoded track, so until such an evaluator exists the encoder keeps emitting Linear and the missing evaluator, not the law, is what constrains the curve. |

| ADR-0073 | art, platform | A slot MAY carry a chain of adjacent ramps — the encoder keeps adjacent ramps, the default fitter emits them and the runtime hands off between them — but a native ramp pays only when it spans 4 or more frames, because one start costs 20.478 us against 6.72 us of frame time per write it replaces, and on the tracked busy fixture the fitter's ramps have a median span of 2 frames so the measured saving comes from HOLD rather than from ramps; wrapping one ramp in a `game.TweenSequence` remains a measured 5.78x loss and is not an optimization target. |

{"file_path":"docs/project/index.md","content":"# project — the project documentation index

Always read this index on entering `docs/project/`. It is the routing table for this repo; there is no other index beside it.

## Routing

| Kind of thing | Home |
| --- | --- |
| A measured platform fact | one row in the template's `miliastra-game-template/docs/project/platform/ref-measurements.md` |
| How to build | `docs/project/building/` |
| A rule that is still true | a `law-` file in `docs/guides/` or a `ref-` file in `docs/project/` — this repo keeps no `docs/specs/` shelf |
| Operating the editor or the game | `docs/project/sessions/` |
| A rule for working on this repo | `docs/guides/` |
| A product or content decision | `docs/adr/` |
| In-flight work | `docs/plans/<date>-<topic>/` until it is settled and moved to its permanent home |
| A raw record | `archive/` — written once, never required reading |

## Naming and size

Three prefixes, on files and on index lines. `law-` is binding: read it before doing the kind of work the filename names. `ref-` is reference: open it only when the task touches the named topic, and it is the default for project knowledge. `work-` is in-flight notes for one effort: no `law-` or `ref-` file ever cites it, and it is settled into a permanent file or moved to `archive/` when the effort ends. This file is where these conventions are stated.

Each document covers one topic, stands alone, and opens with one scope line naming its section. Its body is capped at 150 lines; past that it splits by topic, never by part number, and the split updates this index in the same change. Each fact has exactly one home; other documents link to it instead of repeating it. English and its Chinese counterpart stay inside the same topic document.

### Conventions settled against the template

The template's `docs/project/index.md` states its document conventions differently. Each item below is this repo's choice; the template's wording is not adopted.

- **Body cap.** 150 lines per document, not the template's 250. A document past 150 splits by topic, and this index changes in the same edit.
- **Unit name.** "Document" and "topic", not the template's "chunk" and "concern".
- **Shelf for still-true rules.** This repo keeps no `docs/specs/` shelf: a rule that is still true is a `law-` file in `docs/guides/` or a `ref-` file in `docs/project/`. The template's `docs/specs/` and its entry list are not imported.
- **Path form in index lines.** Cite from the repo root, as `docs/project/building/index.md`, never from the index's own directory. A Markdown link target stays relative to the file that holds the link.
- **`work-` when an effort ends.** Settle it into a permanent file, or move it to `archive/`; the template's "written up or archived" is not adopted.

- `docs/project/ref-glossary.md` — pointer to the glossary and path index at `CONTEXT.md`. Open when a task needs a term's definition, the Avoid list, or the path index.

## Sections

- `docs/project/platform/index.md` — measured platform behavior and this repo's open platform questions. Open when a task needs a measured platform number or an open platform question.

- `docs/project/sessions/index.md` — operating the editor and the game. Open when a task drives the editor or the game.
- `docs/guides/index.md` — procedures for working on this repo. Read before the kind of work a guide names.
"}

{"content":"# ADR index

One line per decision. **Hand-maintained** — there is no generator, so adding an ADR means adding its
row here. Convention: `docs/guides/law-writing-an-adr.md`.

The next number is derived by listing `docs/adr/`, never from this line.

Row grammar: the `Law` cell **mirrors that record's in-force `Law:` line verbatim** — never a summary,
no *Consequences* prose, no re-bolded clause (`docs/guides/law-writing-an-adr.md` § *File anatomy*).
A changed rule is edited in place in its record, so the cell always states what that ADR is now; where
a record carries a `Superseded-by`/`Supersedes` line, the cell adds that one plain cross-reference —
no dated qualifier, no amendment note.

Files in `docs/adr/` today: `ADR-0001-product-names.md`, `ADR-0002-platform-free-core-and-carve-out.md`,
`ADR-0003-carry-over-ratification.md`, `ADR-0004-art-loads-in-source-undecided.md`,
`ADR-0005-code-owned-gameplay-sprites.md`, `ADR-0006-retire-the-phase-gate-condition.md`.

| ID | Topic | Law |
| --- | --- | --- |
| [ADR-0001](ADR-0001-product-names.md) | naming | The product is named EN *Taskworld Project*, CN **Sandbox-City**; `Taskworld-Project` is the repo and code name, internal and never player-facing. |
| [ADR-0002](ADR-0002-platform-free-core-and-carve-out.md) | platform, layout | The platform-free core is Lua naming no platform call, control, save-variable runtime form, coordinate or cap; it may be organised per surface and per shared concern, runs only under this machine's interpreter as a development tool and never a payload dependency, and its 5.1-safe subset is enforced by a static gate module rather than by that runtime — whose 5.4.5 accepts every banned construct. *(superseded in part by ADR-0006 for the phase-gate conditioning clause only)* |
| [ADR-0003](ADR-0003-carry-over-ratification.md) | rules, content | The source game's rules, content and data tables carry over as design seed and nothing else does — no line of code, no file of audio, font or string, and not the previous attempt's genshin-ts toolchain — with the seed corpus's `IMPL_05_DATA_TABLES.md` § *Appendix B* named as the conflict authority for its content figures. |
| [ADR-0004](ADR-0004-art-loads-in-source-undecided.md) | art | Art is loaded into the map as editor image assets and never drawn at runtime, so it costs a budget rather than code; the salvaged example's runtime rect-explosion shape is rejected as the shipping shape, and which art source the project uses stays an open human decision. *(superseded for gameplay sprite ingress/rendering by ADR-0005; superseded in part by ADR-0006 for the phase-gate closure clause)* |
| [ADR-0005](ADR-0005-code-owned-gameplay-sprites.md) | art, platform | Gameplay sprites enter code as data and render through client controls with no external gameplay image upload/import path; cover imagery is outside gameplay, and the data/control budget remains an open A5/A9 human gate. *(supersedes ADR-0004 for gameplay sprite ingress/rendering; superseded in part by ADR-0006 for the phase-gate duration clause)* |
| [ADR-0006](ADR-0006-retire-the-phase-gate-condition.md) | platform, layout | The two decisions conditioned on the phase gate (`ADR-0002` core carve-out, `ADR-0004`/`ADR-0005` art and sprite rulings) stand on their own ground; their gate-conditioning clauses are withdrawn and no rule is weakened. The nine platform questions stay open as questions in `docs/project/platform/ref-platform-facts.md`, unanswerable by no agent and reserved to no human. |
","file_path":"docs/adr/index.md"}

{"content":"# guides — procedures for working on this repo

Always read this index on entering `docs/guides/`. A `law-` file is read before the kind of work it names; a `ref-` file is opened only when the task touches its topic.

- `docs/guides/law-editing-issue-files.md` — numbering, triage, and moves for `issue-tracker/`. Read before creating or editing an issue file.
- `docs/guides/law-writing-an-adr.md` — the parts of a file in `docs/adr/` and how they are numbered. Read before writing or replacing an ADR.
- `docs/guides/law-doing-design-work.md` — what may live under `docs/plans/`. Read before adding anything there.
- `docs/guides/law-scrapping-clutter.md` — the pass that deletes rules, checks and documents an agent invented and nobody asked for: what to delete, what to keep, and how. Read before such a pass, or before writing a rule that might become clutter itself.
- `docs/guides/law-verification-non-vacuity.md` — checks, fixed expected values and file hashes that must be able to fail. Read before adding or extending a check that compares a value with a stored one.
- `docs/guides/law-restoring-exact-bytes.md` — `git checkout` does not restore the exact committed bytes here (autocrlf). Read before putting a changed file back to its committed bytes.
- `docs/guides/law-using-the-official-corpus.md` — starting point for the copied official documents. Read before using one of the copied official documents.
- `docs/guides/ref-corpus-layout.md` — where the copied document folders live and why. Open when a task needs to know where the copies sit.
- `docs/guides/ref-corpus-keying.md` — how each copied file is named and which chapter folder holds it. Open when a task names or places a copied file.
- `docs/guides/ref-corpus-front-matter.md` — the header fields of a copied file, what the corpus forbids, and where this repo's notes stop and the copied text starts. Open when a task adds or cites a copied file's header fields.
- `docs/guides/ref-corpus-locale-pairs.md` — whether the EN and CN copies of one article match, and what a citation must record. Open when a task cites one side of a copied EN/CN pair.
- `docs/guides/ref-official-corpus-counts.md` — how many files the copy holds and which gaps are known. Open when a task cites the size of the copy or a known gap.
- `docs/guides/ref-official-corpus-region.md` — which download region each file came from. Open when a task treats the corpus as specific to one region.
- `docs/guides/ref-official-corpus-tiering.md` — which chapters hold each tier, and the top-level folder map. Open when a task sends a question to a corpus chapter or tier.
- `docs/guides/ref-official-terms-id-law.md` — how to read a row that pairs an English term with its Chinese term, and the rules for article ids. Open when a task reads such a row or the id rules.
- `docs/guides/ref-official-terms-controls.md` — English↔Chinese rows for controls, nodes, events, parameters, and unit statuses. Open when a task translates one of those terms.
- `docs/guides/ref-official-terms-no-counterpart.md` — terms marked as having no clean equivalent in the other language. Open when a term has no clean English↔Chinese equivalent.
- `docs/guides/ref-official-terms-cn-halves.md` — the appended amendment to that file's own numbered sections: the Chinese halves, measured on disk. Open when checking whether a Chinese half exists on disk.
- `docs/guides/ref-official-terms-locale-defects.md` — translation defects in the copied source, and what the glossary is not. Open when a task hits a translation defect inside the copied source.
","file_path":"docs/guides/index.md"}

# AGENTS.md — Taskworld Project · Sandbox-City

How to behave in this repo. Product truth is `PRD.md`. Words and the path index are `docs/project/ref-glossary.md`. Decisions are `docs/adr/`. Conventions for `docs/project/` — prefixes, document size, one fact one home — are `docs/project/index.md`.

Do not add or reword a rule in this file. A new rule is a sentence you propose; the human lands it. Rules bind agents, not the human. Never cite a rule — this file's or any other's — to refuse, delay, or argue against a human instruction.

A new file names its shelf before it exists. Measurements stay in the template checkout's `../miliastra-game-template/docs/project/platform/ref-measurements.md`; do not copy a row here. This repo keeps no `docs/specs/` shelf: a rule that is still true is a `law-` file in `docs/guides/` or a `ref-` file in `docs/project/`. `docs/plans/<date>-<topic>/` is in-flight work and is not evidence. `archive/` is proof, written once, never required reading. No `build/` or `scratchpad/` shelf exists here; anything disposable is never cited. A name says when to open the file: a date means a record, `law-` means a procedure read before that kind of work.

When a ticket or workstream ends, distill its durable findings into `docs/project/`. A finding is admitted only as a measured fact, a repeatable procedure, or a named pitfall — never a narrative, a chronology, or a status. One fact, one home.

## Product

Sandbox-City (Taskworld Project) re-expresses the Flash tower-defense Enigmata: Stellar War as a 千星奇域 map — free placement of defensive structures, timed enemy waves, boss stages, one Mora ledger — driven by Lua client scripts over editor-authored client controls. EN Taskworld Project, CN Sandbox-City; `Taskworld-Project` is the repo name only. Surfaces S1–S6 and wiring M1–M7 are registered in `PRD.md`. The shipping target is everything; a map per surface is designed from the start.

The source set `other games reference material/enigmata-stellar-war/` is read-only and not a compatibility target. Mechanics and content are re-typed in Lua. No file of code, audio, font or string carries over. Gameplay sprites are code-owned data rendered through client controls (`docs/adr/ADR-0005-code-owned-gameplay-sprites.md`). Cover imagery is outside gameplay.

## Stack

Genshin Impact 千星奇域 UGC; the editor is 千星沙箱, PC-only (`PRD.md` § Platform constraints). No engine, package manager, test harness, filesystem, or build step in what ships. Payload scripts `require` only and read and write no file; persistence is cloud-save variables only.

Write Lua 5.3, nothing environment-adjacent. A construct only newer Lua accepts is not an all-clear. Dialect probe: `ISSUE-014`. The runtime supplies no libraries, no LuaJIT, no `load`/`loadstring`. Missing facilities are rewritten in portable Lua.

`platform-free-core/` is the one carve-out (`docs/adr/ADR-0002-platform-free-core-and-carve-out.md`): pure Lua naming no platform call, run under this machine's `lua.exe` as a development tool, never a payload dependency. Module law: `platform-free-core/README.md`. The 5.1-safe subset is policed by `dev/lua-gate/`, not by that interpreter — local Lua 5.4.5 parses what the subset bans (`docs/project/building/ref-lua-subset-gate.md`). A local named exactly `oddx` miscompiles; rename and re-run before believing the failure. A green local run is arithmetic evidence only, never proof the payload loads.

A documented figure is never a designable number. Engine measurements live in the template checkout, at `../miliastra-game-template/docs/project/platform/ref-measurements.md` — an external path, not a file in this repo. A number copied into this repo is stale. Design against a value you confirmed in the editor, and expect it to move.

## Contracts

- A surface's state machine owns phase and outcomes. The control layer only displays them. Logic inside a draw path is a defect.
- Settlement is event-driven. Mora changes on the settle event, never on a clock. Exactly one write seam (`PRD.md` F13, M2).
- Rewrite control text when the fact changes. Never rebuild a surface to change one number.
- Fragile areas — report, do not fix. A change names the invariant: the Mora ledger write (never negative, re-granted at stage start, forfeit on leave) and its save-key namespace; the phase owner (`PRD.md` M1); the structure, enemy, enhancement and stage tables in `PRD.md` § Content of record; the placement-capacity rule (`PRD.md` F4) — eight placed structures including the Command Base.

## Localization

EN and CN are co-equal, authored together. No player-facing literal in code or in an editor text field. Both entries of a key land in the same change. Parity is opening `locale/en.lua` and `locale/zh_cn.lua`. Never import the source game's locale files. Do not quote a remembered key total.

## Verification

The legibility gate (`PRD.md` NFR12) is a human judgement. An agent cannot pass it. Capture is a pre-check, never acceptance. Where you cannot play, say the requirement is unverified. Graceful degradation is `PRD.md` NFR18; the game plays with motion off (NFR13).

## Issues and decisions

File a defect with a failing check under `issue-tracker/open/` before the fix. Do not file a doc or process issue. Do not write a handover file. Numbering and moves: `docs/guides/law-editing-issue-files.md`. An issue file is never deleted.

ADRs are product and content decisions, written before the decision is implemented. Workplace rules are not ADRs. Convention: `docs/guides/law-writing-an-adr.md`. The live list is `docs/adr/index.md`.

`archive/` is proof, never required reading. Do not edit it and do not append inside it.

## Editing

No bulk replace and no tree-wide regex: both have corrupted UTF-8 and CN strings (千星奇域, 千星沙箱, 摩拉). After a multi-file edit, confirm each file still decodes as UTF-8.

Cite paths relative to the repo root. The one sibling path allowed is the template checkout's `../miliastra-game-template/docs/project/platform/ref-measurements.md`; it names a file outside this repo, which is where measurements live. A machine-local absolute needs `<!-- device-path: … -->` on that same block. `file:///` is never used.

One writer per file. A non-owner writes the exact wording into the owning ticket. One git writer per checkout; concurrent lanes may use separate worktrees. Commits are pathspec-limited. No history surgery in a shared checkout.

## Shell and the game

Every shell command has a positive timeout and does only what was asked. Never a watcher, dev server, REPL, or open-ended job. No CI, and do not add one.

Never kill the game process. Exit a playtest in-game: Esc, then 中断挑战, then 离开. Force-kill `YuanShen.exe` only when the game is frozen and that path does not work.

Publishing a map is a human action. Never submit or publish through the Sandbox, and never touch a published map. Push, PRs, tags, and write-scoped `gh` only when the human asks in this conversation.

From the Genshin main menu: Esc, scroll to the bottom, 我的奇域. Esc on an editor tab returns to the editor menu; Esc again toggles the left bar. The third button on that bar is the save-file manager. Turn logging on every time the editor opens, or the session writes no `.gia`: 千星沙箱 window, 窗口 → 日志, scroll 选择单位 to the bottom, tick 客户端脚本. Further click-paths are `docs/project/sessions/law-editor-sessions.md`, and only during a Sandbox session.

## Standing rules
1. Summon subagents in background mode by default.
2. Owner works from 2 devices: one has `C:\Users\AAAAA\`, the other has `C:\Users\TZ\`.
3. Never invent jargon, codenames, or project shorthand. Talk to the human in plain, very concise language, as if he has ADHD: short sentences, concrete words, no metaphors, no private vocabulary. A term that needs explaining to a newcomer is not allowed in a sentence to the owner.
4. Run the smallest test set that can fail. Do not run end-to-end tests when unit tests cover the change. Group tests into one run instead of starting one run per change.

</system-reminder>

Write Lua 5.3, nothing environment-adjacent. A construct only newer Lua accepts is not an all-clear. Dialect probe: `ISSUE-014`. The runtime supplies no libraries, no LuaJIT, no `load`/`loadstring`. Missing facilities are rewritten in portable Lua.

`platform-free-core/` is the one carve-out (`docs/adr/ADR-0002-platform-free-core-and-carve-out.md`): pure Lua naming no platform call, run under this machine's `lua.exe` as a development tool, never a payload dependency. Module law: `platform-free-core/README.md`. The 5.1-safe subset is policed by `dev/lua-gate/`, not by that interpreter — local Lua 5.4.5 parses what the subset bans (`docs/project/building/ref-lua-subset-gate.md`). A local named exactly `oddx` miscompiles; rename and re-run before believing the failure. A green local run is arithmetic evidence only, never proof the payload loads.

A documented figure is never a designable number. Engine measurements live in the template checkout, at `../miliastra-game-template/docs/project/platform/ref-measurements.md` — an external path, not a file in this repo. A number copied into this repo is stale. Design against a value you confirmed in the editor, and expect it to move.

## Contracts

- A surface's state machine owns phase and outcomes. The control layer only displays them. Logic inside a draw path is a defect.
- Settlement is event-driven. Mora changes on the settle event, never on a clock. Exactly one write seam (`PRD.md` F13, M2).
- Rewrite control text when the fact changes. Never rebuild a surface to change one number.
- Fragile areas — report, do not fix. A change names the invariant: the Mora ledger write (never negative, re-granted at stage start, forfeit on leave) and its save-key namespace; the phase owner (`PRD.md` M1); the structure, enemy, enhancement and stage tables in `PRD.md` § 7 *Content of record*; the placement-capacity rule (`PRD.md` F4) — eight placed structures including the Command Base.

## Localization

EN and CN are co-equal, authored together. No player-facing literal in code or in an editor text field. Both entries of a key land in the same change. Parity is opening `locale/en.lua` and `locale/zh_cn.lua`. Never import the source game's locale files. Do not quote a remembered key total.

## Verification

The legibility gate (`PRD.md` NFR12) is a human judgement. An agent cannot pass it. Capture is a pre-check, never acceptance. Where you cannot play, say the requirement is unverified. Graceful degradation is `PRD.md` NFR18; the game plays with motion off (NFR13).

## Issues and decisions

File a defect with a failing check under `issue-tracker/open/` before the fix. Do not file a doc or process issue. Do not write a handover file. Numbering and moves: `docs/guides/law-editing-issue-files.md`. An issue file is never deleted.

ADRs are product and content decisions, written before the decision is implemented. Workplace rules are not ADRs. Convention: `docs/guides/law-writing-an-adr.md`. The live list is `docs/adr/index.md`.

`archive/` is proof, never required reading. Do not edit it and do not append inside it.

## Editing

No bulk replace and no tree-wide regex: both have corrupted UTF-8 and CN strings (千星奇域, 千星沙箱, 摩拉). After a multi-file edit, confirm each file still decodes as UTF-8.

Cite paths relative to the repo root. The one sibling path allowed is the template checkout's `../miliastra-game-template/docs/project/platform/ref-measurements.md`; it names a file outside this repo, which is where measurements live. A machine-local absolute needs `<!-- device-path: … -->` on that same block. `file:///` is never used.

One writer per file. A non-owner writes the exact wording into the owning ticket. One git writer per checkout; concurrent lanes may use separate worktrees. Commits are pathspec-limited. No history surgery in a shared checkout.

## Shell and the game

Every shell command has a positive timeout and does only what was asked. Never a watcher, dev server, REPL, or open-ended job. No CI, and do not add one.

Never kill the game process. Exit a playtest in-game: Esc, then 中断挑战, then 离开. Force-kill `YuanShen.exe` only when the game is frozen and that path does not work.

Publishing a map is a human action. Never submit or publish through the Sandbox, and never touch a published map. Push, PRs, tags, and write-scoped `gh` only when the human asks in this conversation.

From the Genshin main menu: Esc, scroll to the bottom, 我的奇域. Esc on an editor tab returns to the editor menu; Esc again toggles the left bar. The third button on that bar is the save-file manager. Turn logging on every time the editor opens, or the session writes no `.gia`: 千星沙箱 window, 窗口 → 日志, scroll 选择单位 to the bottom, tick 客户端脚本. Further click-paths are `docs/project/sessions/law-editor-sessions.md`, and only during a Sandbox session.

## Standing rules
1. Summon subagents in background mode by default.
2. Owner works from 2 devices: one has `C:\Users\AAAAA\`, the other has `C:\Users\TZ\`.
3. Never invent jargon, codenames, or project shorthand. Talk to the human in plain, very concise language, as if he has ADHD: short sentences, concrete words, no metaphors, no private vocabulary. A term that needs explaining to a newcomer is not allowed in a sentence to the owner.
4. Run the smallest test set that can fail. Do not run end-to-end tests when unit tests cover the change. Group tests into one run instead of starting one run per change.

</system-reminder>
