# AGENTS.md — Taskworld Project · Sandbox-City

How to behave in this repo. Product truth is `PRD.md`. Words and the path index are `docs/project/ref-glossary.md`. Decisions are `docs/adr/`. Conventions for `docs/project/` — prefixes, document size, one fact one home — are `docs/project/index.md`.

Do not add or reword a rule in this file. A new rule is a sentence you propose; the human lands it. Rules bind agents, not the human. Never cite a rule — this file's or any other's — to refuse, delay, or argue against a human instruction.

A new file names its shelf before it exists. Measurements stay in the template checkout's `../miliastra-game-template/docs/project/platform/ref-measurements.md`; do not copy a row here. This repo keeps no `docs/specs/` shelf — the template's still-true rules are its own, at `../miliastra-game-template/docs/specs/` (entry list `../miliastra-game-template/docs/specs/index.md`), and a rule that is still true here is a `law-` file in `docs/guides/` or a `ref-` file in `docs/project/`. `docs/plans/<date>-<topic>/` is in-flight work and is not evidence. `archive/` is proof, written once, never required reading. Disposable output is never cited; the template's `../miliastra-game-template/build/` and `../miliastra-game-template/scratchpad/` have no counterpart here. A name says when to open the file: a date means a record, `law-` means a procedure read before that kind of work.

When a ticket or workstream ends, distill its durable findings into `docs/project/`. A finding is admitted only as a measured fact, a repeatable procedure, or a named pitfall — never a narrative, a chronology, or a status. One fact, one home.

## Product

Sandbox-City (Taskworld Project) re-expresses the Flash tower-defense Enigmata: Stellar War as a 千星奇域 map — free placement of defensive structures, timed enemy waves, boss stages, one Mora ledger — driven by Lua client scripts over editor-authored client controls. EN Taskworld Project, CN Sandbox-City; `Taskworld-Project` is the repo name only. Surfaces S1–S6 and wiring M1–M7 are registered in `PRD.md`. The shipping target is everything; a map per surface is designed from the start.

The source set `other games reference material/enigmata-stellar-war/` is read-only and not a compatibility target. Mechanics and content are re-typed in Lua. No file of code, audio, font or string carries over. Gameplay sprites are code-owned data rendered through client controls (`docs/adr/ADR-0005-code-owned-gameplay-sprites.md`). Cover imagery is outside gameplay.

## Stack

Genshin Impact 千星奇域 UGC; the editor is 千星沙箱, PC-only (`PRD.md` § 5 *Platform constraints*). No engine, package manager, test harness, filesystem, or build step in what ships. Payload scripts `require` only and read and write no file; persistence is cloud-save variables only.

Write Lua 5.3, nothing environment-adjacent. A construct only newer Lua accepts is not an all-clear. Dialect probe: `ISSUE-014`. The runtime supplies no libraries, no LuaJIT, no `load`/`loadstring`. Missing facilities are rewritten in portable Lua.

`platform-free-core/` is the one carve-out (`docs/adr/ADR-0002-platform-free-core-and-carve-out.md`): pure Lua naming no platform call, run under this machine's `lua.exe` as a development tool, never a payload dependency. Module law: `platform-free-core/README.md`. The 5.1-safe subset is policed by `dev/lua-gate/`, not by that interpreter — local Lua 5.4.5 parses what the subset bans (`docs/project/building/ref-lua-subset-gate.md`). A local named exactly `oddx` miscompiles; rename and re-run before believing the failure. A green local run is arithmetic evidence only, never proof the payload loads.

A documented figure is never a designable number. Engine measurements live in the template checkout, at `../miliastra-game-template/docs/project/platform/ref-measurements.md` — an external path, not a file in this repo. A number copied into this repo is stale. Design against a value you confirmed in the editor, and expect it to move.

## Contracts

- A surface's state machine owns phase and outcomes. The control layer only displays them. Logic inside a draw path is a defect.
- Settlement is event-driven. Mora changes on the settle event, never on a clock. Exactly one write seam (`PRD.md` F13, M2).
- Rewrite control text when the fact changes. Never rebuild a surface to change one number.
- Fragile areas — report, do not fix. A change names the invariant: the Mora ledger write (never negative, re-granted at stage start, forfeit on leave) and its save-key namespace; the phase owner (`PRD.md` M1); the structure, enemy, enhancement and stage tables in `PRD.md` § 7 *Content of record*; the placement-capacity rule (`PRD.md` F4) — eight placed structures including the Command Base.

## Localization

EN and CN are co-equal, authored together. No player-facing literal in code or in an editor text field. Both entries of a key land in the same change. Parity is opening `locale/en.lua` and `locale/zh_cn.lua`. Never import the source game's locale files. Do not quote a remembered key total.

## Verification

The legibility gate (`PRD.md` NFR12) is a human judgement. An agent cannot pass it. Capture is a pre-check, never acceptance. Where you cannot play, say the requirement is unverified. Graceful degradation is `PRD.md` NFR18; the game plays with motion off (NFR13).

## Issues and decisions

File a defect with a failing check under `issue-tracker/open/` before the fix. Do not file a doc or process issue. Do not write a handover file. Numbering and moves: `docs/guides/law-editing-issue-files.md`. An issue file is never deleted.

ADRs are product and content decisions, written before the decision is implemented. Workplace rules are not ADRs. Convention: `docs/guides/law-writing-an-adr.md`. The live list is `docs/adr/index.md`.

`archive/` is proof, never required reading. Do not edit it and do not append inside it.

## Editing

No bulk replace and no tree-wide regex: both have corrupted UTF-8 and CN strings (千星奇域, 千星沙箱, 摩拉). After a multi-file edit, confirm each file still decodes as UTF-8.

Cite paths relative to the repo root. The one sibling path allowed is the template checkout's `../miliastra-game-template/docs/project/platform/ref-measurements.md`; it names a file outside this repo, which is where measurements live. A machine-local absolute needs `<!-- device-path: … -->` on that same block. `file:///` is never used.

One writer per file. A non-owner writes the exact wording into the owning ticket. One git writer per checkout; concurrent lanes may use separate worktrees. Commits are pathspec-limited. No history surgery in a shared checkout.

## Shell and the game

Every shell command has a positive timeout and does only what was asked. Never a watcher, dev server, REPL, or open-ended job. No CI, and do not add one.

Never kill the game process. Exit a playtest in-game: Esc, then 中断挑战, then 离开. Force-kill `YuanShen.exe` only when the game is frozen and that path does not work.

Further click-paths are `docs/project/sessions/law-editor-sessions.md`, and only during a Sandbox session.

1. Summon subagents in background mode by default.
2. Owner works from 2 devices: one has `C:\Users\AAAAA\`, the other has `C:\Users\TZ\`.
3. Never invent jargon, codenames, or project shorthand. Talk to the human in plain, very concise language, as if he has ADHD: short sentences, concrete words, no metaphors, no private vocabulary. A term that needs explaining to a newcomer is not allowed in a sentence to the owner.
4. Run the smallest test set that can fail. Do not run end-to-end tests when unit tests cover the change. Group tests into one run instead of starting one run per change.

- No external gameplay image upload/import path and no text-canvas composition; gameplay sprites are code-owned data rendered through client controls (N5, D2).

- No ported Flash code, no genshin-ts/TypeScript pipeline, no node-graph logic for v1 mechanics: the code examples in the seed corpus (the previous attempt's design documents) are read with that caveat; logic is re-typed as Lua client scripts.
- No endless mode, no difficulty tiers beyond the recorded Normal pacing, no stage 6: out of scope, and only a human decision adds them.
- No persistence of in-stage state — balance, placed structures, wave index: a stage is a transaction (F39).
- No audio, fonts or 3D model content in v1 (N4, D1): the game must be fully playable silent (NFR13, NFR14).
- No mobile authoring or mobile acceptance target: the editor is PC-only (5.1); play on mobile is a look.
## 4. Product pillars
The small set of promises every design decision is checked against.
1. Readable command — the field reads as facts, not as motion. If a player cannot tell phase, balance, wave and threat apart at a glance, the surface is re-scoped, not animated harder.
2. One economy, one owner — the Mora (摩拉) ledger is one number changed by named events at one seam (F13); no display path, timer or animation may mint or burn it (NFR6, NFR10).

3. Economy posture — no real-money or platform-currency path anywhere: cosmetic-only stakes, no purchase path, no payout of any kind. Weaken it only by a human decision recorded in its own N row and, if it changes architecture, its own ADR.
## 5. Platform constraints
### 5.1 What the build must live inside
| Constraint | Consequence for this product |

| Logic is Lua client scripts, driving client controls authored in the editor. | The whole game is scripts plus control layouts. No engine, no framework, no build step, no platform libraries or vendor modules at runtime: a facility the runtime does not supply is rewritten in portable Lua (`AGENTS.md`, Stack and platform). |

| Client-local and server-side are separate domains. | Single-player logic may sit client-local; anything whose outcome must match for all players lives in a server-side graph. Nothing shared-stake is designed before the multiplayer decision (R3, D3). |

| The simultaneous-visible-control budget is the binding constraint. | All surfaces share one visible-control budget; hiding a whole group is the only relief valve, and whether a script may do it is A7. If it may not, the split-map fallback (section 8.3) is the plan, not an emergency. |

| Gameplay sprites are code-owned data rendered through client controls. | No external gameplay image upload/import path exists. The measured sprite-data and control capacity lives in `../miliastra-game-template/docs/project/platform/ref-measurements.md`; design against it. Cover imagery is outside gameplay. |

| Persistence is cloud-save variables only. No filesystem, no file I/O; whether `require` spans files is unresolved. | Persistent state is a variable with a capacity budget; a key registry with version stamps is needed before the first key is written (NFR16); save scope is A8. |

| Caps are documented, unit-less and scope-unconfirmed; the editor is PC-only. | Every printed cap digit is documentation, never a designable number — each is an early verification task (5.2), and layouts are designed against confirmed answers only. Playtesting on mobile is a look, not an edit. |

What the device has actually measured — layout, the tick, per-control text, runtime control creation, the caps and the sprite budget — lives in `../miliastra-game-template/docs/project/platform/ref-measurements.md`, and what remains unknown — cross-session save, group show/hide, cloud-save scope — is kept as open questions in `docs/project/platform/ref-platform-facts.md`. Design against the measured rows in ENGINE.md; the open questions have one `Type: research` issue each, and each resolves into an ADR where the answer changes architecture. ## 6. Functional requirements

The acceptance column is a human instruction, not a test: a person can pass or fail the row in 千星沙箱 by doing what the row says, on the row's surface, with no tooling attached. What an agent may verify is narrow — arithmetic, wave ordering, AI policy and economy totals, executed in `platform-free-core/` under the local interpreter; no agent may claim that a screen reads, that a face is legible, that a layout fits, that a control budget held, or that persistence worked across a real session (`AGENTS.md`, Visual verification). Requirement IDs are append-only: a withdrawn item keeps its number.

ID conventions: bare, dot-free identifiers, each in one registry — F functional requirement (6.1); G goal (3.1); N product posture row (6.5); NFR non-functional requirement (6.4); R standing rule (6.6); A platform assumption (5.2); D open product decision (6.7); S surface (6.2); M wiring piece (6.3). IDs are never reused for a different meaning.

## 7. Content of record

Seed-derived starting values to be tuned, never platform facts (R1, NFR17). These tables are the single source of numbers for this product (a fragile area); per-wave compositions live in the seed corpus, in `DESIGN_UGC_02_DATA_MODEL.md` and `DESIGN_UGC_05_ENEMY_WAVES.md` under `docs/plans/2026-05-27-previous-attempt-design-corpus/`.
### 7.1 Structures
The seven buildable types plus the authored base.

### 7.2 Cadence and economy constants
Authored in seconds (R5); the master-loop row is the seed's own reading at its nominal tick rate.
| Constant | Value of record |
| Master loop rate (seed reading only) | 33 ms / about 30 ticks/s — not a platform figure; A2 owns it |
| Economy accrual beat | 5.0 s; 50 Mora per vault per beat |

### 7.3 Enhancements
Cost of level n = `baseCost + costScale × (n − 1)`.

### 7.4 Enemies, stages and waves

Enemy roster: 18 types — trash 100-104, standard 110-114, elite 120-122, flying 130-132, boss 150-151 — with HP, speed, attack, armour, Mora reward and behaviour per the seed corpus's data model. Bosses: 150 Azar — Star Devourer, 3000 HP, armour 10, reward 500, two phases, escorts and nova under 50% HP; 151 Krohn — Infernal Forge, 5000 HP, armour 15, reward 800, two phases. Flying enemies arrive from Stage 4.

### 7.5 Talents and items

Six active talents, cost / cooldown (duration where it differs): Meteor 2000 / 60 s · Healing Wave 800 / 45 s · Deploy Barrier 600 / 30 s (15 s) · Overcharge 1500 / 90 s (15 s) · Sentry Drone 1000 / 60 s (30 s) · Time Slow 1200 / 75 s (8 s).

Eight items: three Mora pouches (50 / 150 / 500), Attack Elixir, Swift Tonic, Aether Charm, Storm Lord's Wrath, Shadow Barrier; drop weights by enemy tier per the seed corpus's items doc (`DESIGN_UGC_07_ITEMS_TALENTS.md`).
### 7.6 Rank and achievements

Rank thresholds 0 / 500 / 1500 / 4000 / 10000 EXP, per-run only; the top tier's compound multipliers are ×1.38 HP, ×1.44 damage, ×1.50 range. Seven achievements pay 500 / 2000 / 1000 / 1000 / 1500 / 2000 / 5000 Mora once each, on their named events (F37).
### 7.7 Terms and strings

- `CONTEXT.md` is the term authority; the seed corpus's replacement glossary (`docs/plans/2026-05-27-previous-attempt-design-corpus/GLOSSARY_REPLACEMENTS.md`) is a candidate map adopted term by term, never wholesale.

- Every player-visible string is one key with an authored EN and an authored CN entry created in the same change (F40, NFR1, NFR2); the locale files are `locale/en.lua` and `locale/zh_cn.lua`, and the key count's home is `docs/project/building/ref-locale-denominator.md`.
- Never import the source game's or the previous attempt's locale files: agreed terminology is the reference; keys, layout and accessor never are.
## 8. Phasing, exit criteria and the split-map fallback
### 8.1 Phasing

- Phase 0 — a short investigation. It settles the open questions and builds almost nothing. Measure the open platform questions in writing (one research issue each), run the test procedures in `docs/project/building/phase0-protocols/`, record every measured figure together with the work pass that measured it, and choose one of two routes: a single map, or the split-map fallback. Close the open decisions (D1, D2, D7) to the extent a human will; the platform-free core (the economy code, the tables, the wave scheduler and the random-number generator) is organised and exercised during Phase 0.

- Phase 1 — build the surfaces in parallel. One surface per owner, no two owners touching the same files, and nothing published in this phase — a half-built hub is not a map. Order does not matter; the wiring (M1-M7) is integrated last, and the integration owner is responsible for those wiring rows.
- Phase 2 — integrate, and publish once. Publication is one event, allowed only when the whole set passes (8.2); the publishing checklist is handed to the human, who alone publishes.
### 8.2 Whole-set exit criteria
The set a human reads before consenting to publication. Every row is pass/fail by playing; no row may be marked passed on the strength of an agent's own mockup.
1. Every 6.2 surface row passes its acceptance check and its NFR12 gate on the real map, in both locales.
2. Every 6.3 wiring row passes: one ledger (M2), one phase owner (M1), one persisted key registry (M4).
3. Every F-row's acceptance has been walked by a person who did not write it, in order, S1 to S6.
4. NFR1-NFR18 hold, or name their exception in writing; NFR12's gate has a dated human verdict beside it.

5. The platform questions of 5.2 are measured, each resolving into an ADR where the answer changes architecture — an unanswered question that a row depends on is a blocked publication, not a risk note.
6. Both locale key sets are identical, verified by opening both files, and the count is stamped at its home (`docs/project/building/ref-locale-denominator.md`).
7. D1, D2 and D7 are decided; where D2 is still open, no final gameplay sprite-data set claim may be made and the set fails.
8. A playtest path exists for all five stages end to end, silent and motion-off (NFR13, NFR14).
9. No row in this file cites an unconfirmed platform figure as its basis (R1, NFR17).
10. The creator-facing policy reading has happened by a human, and its name, version and date are recorded.
### 8.3 The split-map fallback — designed for from the start

If A7 answers that a script may not show and hide whole control groups, or if A5's confirmed count cannot hold S1-S6 at once, each surface becomes its own map with S1 as the entry point. Planned from the start, not used as a last resort:

- The economy stays in-run either way: Mora is session-scoped (F21), so the split never splits the balance; what the split threatens is read-back, and A8 decides whether one persisted key set survives across maps. If A8 answers per map, the progression data families (F36) must be given a new place or the campaign restructured — a scope change decided by a human, never absorbed silently.

- Cost named in advance: the phase driver (M1), ledger seam (M2) and the locale lookup (M7) are duplicated per map, and every hand-off between maps becomes an authored entry point rather than a show/hide.
- The exit criterion that changes: 8.2 row 1 is then checked per map, and row 5's A5/A7/A8 answers are the evidence attached to the decision.

lines.text: # ADR-0003 — what carries from *Enigmata: Stellar War* and the previous attempt, and what never does
Status: **Accepted** (2026-09-28 — the overnight meta wave's instantiation instruction; `AGENTS.md`
§ *What this project is* and § *Never carried over* name this slot, and its bullet list opens with the two
rows this record ratifies)
Topic: rules, content

Law: The source game's rules, content and data tables carry over as design seed and nothing else does — no line of code, no file of audio, font or string, and not the previous attempt's genshin-ts toolchain — with the seed corpus's `IMPL_05_DATA_TABLES.md` § *Appendix B* named as the conflict authority for its content figures.
## Context
`AGENTS.md:22` states that "the single **Mora** (摩拉) ledger and the original's content carry over
(`<carry-over ADR id>` …)" and `AGENTS.md` § *Never carried over* forbids importing the origin's *plumbing*
with its *rules*; both await this project's own record.
The origin is held read-only as `other games reference material/enigmata-stellar-war/`. Its engine shape is
documented there: a **parallel-array entity component system** (`…/00_OVERVIEW.md:18`), whose index soup is
named in the loop analysis — `allXc`, `allYc` as `Vector.<Number>` world-space coordinate arrays, a dead
entity flagged by `allAlive[i] = false` with its coordinates teleported to the `-1441` sentinel
(`…/01_GAME_LOOP.md:119`, `:153`) — all of it living on the decompiled `MainTimeline.as`
(`…/decompiled-flash-source/scripts/EnigmataTD_fla/MainTimeline.as`). Its timing is **frame** timing: "all
timers count in frames (24-30 FPS)", scaled by `iA[339]/24`, with the player toggling 24 fps against 30 fps
(`…/00_OVERVIEW.md:42`, `…/05_ITEMS_SKILLS_ECONOMY.md:262`).
The seed corpus is the previous attempt's design layer, `docs/plans/2026-05-27-previous-attempt-design-corpus/`,
whose entry README states the two standing caveats this record inherits: the corpus's language line is
*TypeScript (genshin-ts SDK)*, roughly 40% of its IMPL examples reference APIs that do not exist, and its
`API_MIGRATION.md` mapping was deliberately **not** copied
(`…/README.md:20-25`); and every engine figure it prints is documentation, never a designable number
(`…/README.md:26-29`). It also names the economy this project adopts: Mora, single currency, no premium or
gacha path (`…/DESIGN_UGC_MASTER.md:44`).
**Conflict resolution in that corpus is real and measured.** `IMPL_05_DATA_TABLES.md` § *Appendix B*
(`:1318-1347`) exists precisely to reconcile DESIGN_UGC_02 against DESIGN_UGC_04, row by row: the enhancement
cost formula (B.1, kept at DESIGN_UGC_02's `baseCost + costScale × (level − 1)`), the stage-completion bonus
(B.2), the Mora Vault income model (B.3, resolved to the economy-tick model and the
`MORA_VAULT_GEN_PER_TICK = 3` game-tick constant deleted), the enhancement grand total (B.4, `33,900` against
DESIGN_UGC_02 § 4.3's `33,400` prose typo, verified by per-row addition), and the deleted
`INTERMISSION_MORA_BONUS` (B.5). The downstream carrier confirms the resolutions actually landed:
`IMPL_06_ECONOMY_ENHANCE.md:1376-1377` states `ENHANCEMENT_GRAND_TOTAL = 33900`, and its stage-bonus table at
`:1225-1231` carries `300/500/800/1000/1500`. Talents follow a different authority — DESIGN_UGC_07's own status
line, "CANONICAL — supersedes all prior items/talents documents"
(`…/DESIGN_UGC_07_ITEMS_TALENTS.md:6`) — not Appendix B.
## Decision
1. **Rules, content and data tables carry; code does not.** The origin's mechanics and the seed corpus's
numbers are *design seed* — read for rules, data and pacing (`…/README.md:24-25`). Not one line of the
decompiled ActionScript, nor any line of the corpus's TypeScript, enters this project's Lua
(`AGENTS.md` § *Never carried over*). No file of audio, font or string carries either; those media stay
under the import ban until the PRD's open-decision row rules otherwise (ADR-0004 § *Decision*, clause 5).
2. **One economy: Mora.** A single currency, no premium and no gacha path (`…/DESIGN_UGC_MASTER.md:44`), one
ledger with exactly one write seam and no per-surface wallet (`AGENTS.md` § *Contracts that hold whichever
way A1–A9 resolve*). ADR-0003 ratifies the *token and its singularity*; the PRD's economy rows own its
numbers, and the corpus's `Mora` terminology is already the project's (`CONTEXT.md` § *Economy and round*).
3. **The genshin-ts toolchain is never carried.** No TypeScript, no node-graph-as-logic-layer for the client
half, no `API_MIGRATION.md`-style name mapping, no build step (`…/README.md:20-25`; `AGENTS.md`
§ *Stack & platform*). Where the corpus's IMPL snippets show a node-graph call, the rule they encode is
re-typed as a Lua client script or dropped.
4. **The parallel-array ECS is re-typed, not ported.** Entities become explicit Lua tables keyed by the
rule-level identity the core owns (surface key, seat index, card code — never a platform handle, per
ADR-0002 clause 1), each carrying its own named fields; coordinate/index arrays, `allAlive` slot recycling
and the `-1441` sentinel are Flash's memory-shape workaround for a GC-poor VM and get no analogue here. The
enemy stream is authored as a **data-driven wave spec** (a table of waves, groups, spawn timings and boss
rows the PRD tunes), replacing the origin's continuous per-timer spawning; that is a deliberate re-typing,
and the origin's own analysis flags the difference (`…/00_OVERVIEW.md` § *Key Design Insights*, carried in
`CONTEXT.md` § *Wave*).
5. **Content-figure conflict authority.** Where the seed corpus disagrees with itself about a *content* number,
`IMPL_05_DATA_TABLES.md` § *Appendix B* decides, per its own resolutions as written — which means
**DESIGN_UGC_02's stage-bonus row (300/500/800/1000/1500) is carried and DESIGN_UGC_04's higher row
(500/800/1200/1800/2500) is not**, B.2's "IMPL_06 may override at runtime" clause never having been taken up
(`IMPL_05_DATA_TABLES.md:1339`; `IMPL_06_ECONOMY_ENHANCE.md:1225-1231`); the enhancement grand total is
`33,900`; the Mora Vault is the economy-tick model; `INTERMISSION_MORA_BONUS` does not exist. Talents follow
DESIGN_UGC_07's CANONICAL status line, not Appendix B. Anyone re-tuning one of these rows does it in the
PRD and says so there — this record fixes the authority, not a licence to re-derive the numbers from
memory.
6. **Engine figures in the carried material are not platform facts.** The origin's 24–30 fps frame loop
(`…/00_OVERVIEW.md:42`) and the corpus's "`~30 ticks/second`" cooldown note
(`IMPL_05_DATA_TABLES.md:651`) describe a Flash runtime. They carry as *content* pacing intent at most, and
never as a cadence to design against: this project has no confirmed tick at all until **A2** answers, and
`IMPL_05_DATA_TABLES.md:651` itself notes the platform's timer API takes seconds — a documented reading,
unconfirmed in-editor. Likewise every cap the corpus quotes (its `IMPL_07_NODE_BUDGET.md`) stays
documentation, per `AGENTS.md`'s rule against building against a remembered platform figure.
## Consequences
- This record is the value for `AGENTS.md:22`'s `<carry-over ADR id>`.
- Wave and entity design has a shape to write down before code: the Lua entity table set and the wave-spec
schema belong to the PRD's data rows and then to the platform-free core (ADR-0002), where they are pure
tables over plain data — no index arrays, no slot recycling, no clock.
- A reader of the seed corpus now has one sentence of instruction: read Appendix B before trusting any
DESIGN_UGC_02-vs-04 number, and read `README.md`'s caveats before trusting any IMPL snippet.
- Open and named: **A2** (does a periodic update path exist, at what cadence) decides whether any tick-derived
pacing in the carried tables is even expressible; **A6/A8** decide what the Mora ledger may persist; the
PRD's economy and wave rows own every designable value this record merely points at. Nothing here closes an
A-row, and the corpus's own rule that no ADR is written from a page cited there
(`…/README.md:26-29`) holds — this record decides *carriage*, and cites the corpus only for content
authority and provenance.

2. **Organisation is not withheld.** The core may be laid out per surface and per shared concern. What
`AGENTS.md` opens as a question is *layout* — screens, controls, scene and asset trees (see
`docs/specs/platform-facts.md` § *Open questions*) — and a pure-rule
module claims none of it (`platform-free-core/README.md` § *The no-source-layout law*). This is the
`<organisation ADR id>` of `CONTEXT.md:38`.
3. **The interpreter is a development tool, never a project dependency.** It ships nothing and no artifact
requires it (`docs/read-before-agent-ops.md:24-29`).
4. **A static gate module enforces the subset.** Because the runtime cannot (Context above), the 5.1-safe
subset is policed by a gate that *reads source text*, not by a green run: a tool that scans every
`platform-free-core/**/*.lua` file outside `dev/` for the banned constructs, for `io`/`os` use in a module,
and for the two silent-divergence traps, run under the same carve-out, its red line recorded and never
hidden. It is **required and not yet on disk** — measured: this directory held `README.md`,
`example_module.lua`, `dev/run_tests.lua` at `7e52c97` — and it is the deliverable of
`issue-tracker/open/ISSUE-026-open-lua-subset-and-io-linter-tool.md` (file wall `dev/lua-gate/**`), the
ticket this record answers for the findings recorded in `ISSUE-014` (the 5.4.5 run), `ISSUE-015` (the
`io`/`os` ban unenforced locally) and `ISSUE-016` (the stdlib blacklist contradicting the shipped example
maps). Its hand-checked per-module table stays the `NOTES.md`-style design record
`docs/read-before-agent-ops.md:417-422` already demands; the gate automates that record, it does not
replace the reading.
5. **Dev-tool directories are sanctioned tracked tools, and the permission is one-way.** The carve-out covers
`platform-free-core/dev/` and any development tool this project's own tickets place beside it — the runner
`dev/run_tests.lua` may do what a tool does (file reads, a non-zero exit; its guarded `os.exit` at
`platform-free-core/dev/run_tests.lua:53`), and so does the gate of clause 4 wherever its ticket's file wall
puts it (`dev/lua-gate/**`, per `ISSUE-026`). **No shipping payload module and no platform-free-core module
`require`s anything under a `dev/` tree**, and no payload file reads or writes a file (`AGENTS.md`
§ *Stack & platform*); nothing under `dev/` is a dependency shelf, and the vendored `node_modules` already
sitting in `dev/beyond-simulator/` stays the tracked-tooling defect `ISSUE-013` records rather than becoming
a precedent for shipping a dependency. Measured 2026-09-28: the runner as it stands writes no file, resolves
its modules through `package.path` and prints `checks=8 failures=0 / PASS` for the shipped example.
6. **Write to the strictest reading of the disputed stdlib.** Where the editions contradict each other, the
core provides its own portable Lua for `floor`, `ceil`, `sqrt`, `abs`, `min`, `max`, `mod`, `random` (seeded,
in/out per `docs/read-before-agent-ops.md:423-429`) and `shuffle`, and treats `math.*` as *possibly absent*
rather than as a dependency to wait for (`AGENTS.md` § *Stack & platform*, "The runtime hands you nothing").
7. **`fengari` is an optional later cross-check, not a dependency.** Nothing in `platform-free-core/` may
require it, and no build or test pipeline is built on it; a second reader's verdict may be recorded as dated
evidence when someone chooses to run one.
## Consequences
- This record is the value for `AGENTS.md:73` and `:133`'s `<platform-free-core ADR id>`, for both ids in
`CONTEXT.md:36-42` (its § *Platform-free core* term row) — the integrator lands those edits; this wave's file
wall does not include them. The `<carve-out ADR id>` slot in `platform-free-core/README.md`
§ *The carve-out law* is filled inside this same change.
- The core's merge gate now has two halves: `checks=N failures=0` from the runner **and** a green line from the
static gate. Until the gate exists, the hand-checked subset table alone carries the burden, and a module
landing without either is a defect.
- Portable `math` shims are core work, not a shortcut: the shuffle, the seeded generator and the arithmetic
helpers are this project's code by design.
- Open, and named: the device dialect (the `issue-tracker/open/` dialect probe, whose in-editor half no agent
may close), the real per-file script-size cap and what it does to the comment-shadowing ruling
(`docs/read-before-agent-ops.md:373-378`), and every A1–A9 row — this record closes none of them, and no
clause above implies a confirmed platform figure.

| ADR-0007 | tooling, rules | The compressor's approximation search is a plateau-stopped heuristic, never an exhaustive search: it terminates at the first verified non-improving candidate minimum — a content-based, deterministic rule, never wall-clock — toward the owner's expectation of roughly 10 seconds even for large high-resolution input, an expectation still unmet on the 256/512 classes and open on ISSUE-037. |

| ADR-0008 | tooling | Working resolution is an aspect-preserving max-dimension downscale dial — the filter is the `intake_resample` dial (NEAREST default, BOX the measured opt-in, ADR-0020), user-adjustable, default 128, identity when both sides are within the dial, applied to the whole image with no tiling — and one rule governs everywhere: the converter's `max_dimension` recipe key, imported (never copied) by every other consumer. |

| ADR-0009 | tooling, rules | A single-image run over 30 seconds in tests is terminated and drives an optimization obligation through deterministic depth levers — 30 seconds being a testing allowance only, with production targets of at most a few seconds per image worst case and real-time (~24 fps) for typical images on hardware worse than the dev machine's — and the budget lives only in the harness layer as wall-clock, never inside engine decisions. |

| ADR-0010 | tooling | The converter's palette handling is adaptive: source colours quantize at a default depth of 64 and merge down toward at most 16 by integer RGB similarity — merging only spatially neighbouring patches (or folding tiny specks), never non-similar or non-neighbouring ones — as a cheap pre-search converter pass, switched ON by default with every knob dial-able or switchable off (ADR-0015), and with in-search merge moves deferred. *(superseded by ADR-0015 for its opt-in landing shape and default-flip gate only)* |

| ADR-0011 | tooling, art | The engine's shape vocabulary — `rect`, `tri`, `rrect` — is kernel-faithful end-to-end: candidates are priced by the kernel's own rasterization rules, every committed op kind is paintable by every renderer mirror, and generation emits only kernel-valid candidates — one vocabulary, one set of rules, everywhere: engine, preview, harness. |

| ADR-0012 | tooling | The image→drawing browser UI keeps a single search kernel — the real Python engine imported in-process — and the browser only renders: it paints exactly the committed op sequence, in commit order, through the parity-checked renderer (raster.js); a JavaScript search port is rejected as a forking kernel. |

| ADR-0013 | art, tooling | Ring ops are suspended from all output deliverables (demo, previews) by construction — the ring vocabulary, its unmeasured 62% inner-radius rule and every switch that could emit a ring are deleted, the named refusals and the convention kernel's explicit-radii annulus primitive are retained for a rebuild from measured radii — and the suspension lifts only when the diagonal/rotated-shape fitter work passes the owner's 2×-bound 30° diagonal test and a visual re-evaluation follows. *(superseded by ADR-0011 for the whole record)* |

| ADR-0014 | tooling | The product approximation pipeline is greedy-only — no rate-distortion (λ) selection exists in any product path or product-facing default — and the dispatcher survives only as research tooling in `dev/approx-proto` with its frozen oracle, explicitly marked research-only, never shipped in a game. |

| ADR-0015 | tooling | The converter's colour pipeline is, by default, quantize-to-64 (the palette dial, dial-able to any value 1..256 through `palette.colors`) followed by the adaptive merge stage switched ON (source depth = the dial, target 16, threshold 900, speck fold on, every knob dial-able or switchable off through the existing recipe keys) — a separate stage that always runs between quantize and the shape approximation and never inside the search. |

| ADR-0016 | save, tooling | Op-list payloads save in a columnar format (ops split by kind, per-field columns, standard zigzag, x/y deltas, kind-RLE, per-column same-as-previous elision) whose default dialect is per-column static canonical Huffman with code lengths in the header, with LZ4-block as the `lz4-compat` dialect over the same packed stream and the fmtver-1 Lua text module as the `text` debug dialect. |

| ADR-0017 | art, tooling | One converter encodes two drawing-method recipes, chosen at encode time — anim is the DEFAULT (frame 0 ships as a full-program I-frame that instantiates a persistent client-control pool; later frames ship as P-frame mutation lists: exact matches persist at zero cost, near matches become at most 5 property-sets over x/y/w/h/colour, new content creates controls, stale content retires by HIDE) and static draw is OPT-IN, useful only when total game size is in strain (the whole frame ships and is drawn as one program per update — a drawing method, never a load-once lifecycle); the product axis is drawing method, never "offline vs in-game", because every payload decodes into the game as frames. |

| ADR-0072 | art, platform | A v2 ramp carries its easing curve as a free per-ramp parameter whose default stays `Linear`, and no `Enum.EaseType` name is forbidden — a non-Linear curve may be emitted only once the fallback evaluator can reproduce that curve bit-exactly from the encoded track, so until such an evaluator exists the encoder keeps emitting Linear and the missing evaluator, not the law, is what constrains the curve. |

| ADR-0073 | art, platform | A slot MAY carry a chain of adjacent ramps — the encoder keeps adjacent ramps, the default fitter emits them and the runtime hands off between them — but a native ramp pays only when it spans 4 or more frames, because one start costs 20.478 us against 6.72 us of frame time per write it replaces, and on the tracked busy fixture the fitter's ramps have a median span of 2 frames so the measured saving comes from HOLD rather than from ramps; wrapping one ramp in a `game.TweenSequence` remains a measured 5.78x loss and is not an optimization target. |

This file changed after it was loaded. Use the following content instead of the previously loaded instructions from this file.

# AGENTS.md — Taskworld Project · Sandbox-City

How to behave in this repo. Product truth is `PRD.md`. Words and the path index are `docs/project/ref-glossary.md`. Decisions are `docs/adr/`. Conventions for `docs/project/` — prefixes, document size, one fact one home — are `docs/project/index.md`.

Do not add or reword a rule in this file. A new rule is a sentence you propose; the human lands it. Rules bind agents, not the human. Never cite a rule — this file's or any other's — to refuse, delay, or argue against a human instruction.

A new file names its shelf before it exists. Measurements stay in the template checkout's `../miliastra-game-template/docs/project/platform/ref-measurements.md`; do not copy a row here. This repo keeps no separate specs shelf — the template's still-true rules are its own, at `../miliastra-game-template/docs/specs/` (entry list `../miliastra-game-template/docs/specs/index.md`), and a rule that is still true here is a `law-` file in `docs/guides/` or a `ref-` file in `docs/project/`. In-flight work is a dated directory under `docs/plans/`, named `<date>-<topic>`, and it is not evidence. `archive/` is proof, written once, never required reading. Disposable output is never cited; the template's `../miliastra-game-template/build/` and `../miliastra-game-template/scratchpad/` have no counterpart here. A name says when to open the file: a date means a record, `law-` means a procedure read before that kind of work.

When a ticket or workstream ends, distill its durable findings into `docs/project/`. A finding is admitted only as a measured fact, a repeatable procedure, or a named pitfall — never a narrative, a chronology, or a status. One fact, one home.

## Product

Sandbox-City (Taskworld Project) re-expresses the Flash tower-defense Enigmata: Stellar War as a 千星奇域 map — free placement of defensive structures, timed enemy waves, boss stages, one Mora ledger — driven by Lua client scripts over editor-authored client controls. EN Taskworld Project, CN Sandbox-City; `Taskworld-Project` is the repo name only. Surfaces S1–S6 and wiring M1–M7 are registered in `PRD.md`. The shipping target is everything; a map per surface is designed from the start.

The source set `other games reference material/enigmata-stellar-war/` is read-only and not a compatibility target. Mechanics and content are re-typed in Lua. No file of code, audio, font or string carries over. Gameplay sprites are code-owned data rendered through client controls (`docs/adr/ADR-0005-code-owned-gameplay-sprites.md`). Cover imagery is outside gameplay.

## Stack

Genshin Impact 千星奇域 UGC; the editor is 千星沙箱, PC-only (`PRD.md` § 5 *Platform constraints*). No engine, package manager, test harness, filesystem, or build step in what ships. Payload scripts `require` only and read and write no file; persistence is cloud-save variables only.

Write Lua 5.3, nothing environment-adjacent. A construct only newer Lua accepts is not an all-clear. Dialect probe: `ISSUE-014`. The runtime supplies no libraries, no LuaJIT, no `load`/`loadstring`. Missing facilities are rewritten in portable Lua.

`platform-free-core/` is the one carve-out (`docs/adr/ADR-0002-platform-free-core-and-carve-out.md`): pure Lua naming no platform call, run under this machine's `lua.exe` as a development tool, never a payload dependency. Module law: `platform-free-core/README.md`. The 5.1-safe subset is policed by `dev/lua-gate/`, not by that interpreter — local Lua 5.4.5 parses what the subset bans (`docs/project/building/ref-lua-subset-gate.md`). A local named exactly `oddx` miscompiles; rename and re-run before believing the failure. A green local run is arithmetic evidence only, never proof the payload loads.

A documented figure is never a designable number. Engine measurements live in the template checkout, at `../miliastra-game-template/docs/project/platform/ref-measurements.md` — an external path, not a file in this repo. A number copied into this repo is stale. Design against a value you confirmed in the editor, and expect it to move.

## Contracts

- A surface's state machine owns phase and outcomes. The control layer only displays them. Logic inside a draw path is a defect.
- Settlement is event-driven. Mora changes on the settle event, never on a clock. Exactly one write seam (`PRD.md` F13, M2).
- Rewrite control text when the fact changes. Never rebuild a surface to change one number.
- Fragile areas — report, do not fix. A change names the invariant: the Mora ledger write (never negative, re-granted at stage start, forfeit on leave) and its save-key namespace; the phase owner (`PRD.md` M1); the structure, enemy, enhancement and stage tables in `PRD.md` § 7 *Content of record*; the placement-capacity rule (`PRD.md` F4) — eight placed structures including the Command Base.

## Localization

EN and CN are co-equal, authored together. No player-facing literal in code or in an editor text field. Both entries of a key land in the same change. Parity is opening `locale/en.lua` and `locale/zh_cn.lua`. Never import the source game's locale files. Do not quote a remembered key total.

## Verification

The legibility gate (`PRD.md` NFR12) is a human judgement. An agent cannot pass it. Capture is a pre-check, never acceptance. Where you cannot play, say the requirement is unverified. Graceful degradation is `PRD.md` NFR18; the game plays with motion off (NFR13).

## Issues and decisions

File a defect with a failing check under `issue-tracker/open/` before the fix. Do not file a doc or process issue. Do not write a handover file. Numbering and moves: `docs/guides/law-editing-issue-files.md`. An issue file is never deleted.

ADRs are product and content decisions, written before the decision is implemented. Workplace rules are not ADRs. Convention: `docs/guides/law-writing-an-adr.md`. The live list is `docs/adr/index.md`.

`archive/` is proof, never required reading. Do not edit it and do not append inside it.

## Editing

No bulk replace and no tree-wide regex: both have corrupted UTF-8 and CN strings (千星奇域, 千星沙箱, 摩拉). After a multi-file edit, confirm each file still decodes as UTF-8.

Cite paths relative to the repo root. The one sibling path allowed is the template checkout's `../miliastra-game-template/docs/project/platform/ref-measurements.md`; it names a file outside this repo, which is where measurements live. A machine-local absolute needs `<!-- device-path: … -->` on that same block. `file:///` is never used.

One writer per file. A non-owner writes the exact wording into the owning ticket. One git writer per checkout; concurrent lanes may use separate worktrees. Commits are pathspec-limited. No history surgery in a shared checkout.

## Shell and the game

Every shell command has a positive timeout and does only what was asked. Never a watcher, dev server, REPL, or open-ended job. No CI, and do not add one.

Never kill the game process. Exit a playtest in-game: Esc, then 中断挑战, then 离开. Force-kill `YuanShen.exe` only when the game is frozen and that path does not work.

Publishing a map is a human action. Never submit or publish through the Sandbox, and never touch a published map. Push, PRs, tags, and write-scoped `gh` only when the human asks in this conversation.

From the Genshin main menu: Esc, scroll to the bottom, 我的奇域. Esc on an editor tab returns to the editor menu; Esc again toggles the left bar. The third button on that bar is the save-file manager. Turn logging on every time the editor opens, or the session writes no `.gia`: 千星沙箱 window, 窗口 → 日志, scroll 选择单位 to the bottom, tick 客户端脚本. Further click-paths are `docs/project/sessions/law-editor-sessions.md`, and only during a Sandbox session.

## Standing rules
1. Summon subagents in background mode by default.
2. Owner works from 2 devices: one has `C:\Users\AAAAA\`, the other has `C:\Users\TZ\`.
3. Never invent jargon, codenames, or project shorthand. Talk to the human in plain, very concise language, as if he has ADHD: short sentences, concrete words, no metaphors, no private vocabulary. A term that needs explaining to a newcomer is not allowed in a sentence to the owner.
4. Run the smallest test set that can fail. Do not run end-to-end tests when unit tests cover the change. Group tests into one run instead of starting one run per change.

</system-reminder>

# AGENTS.md — Taskworld Project · Sandbox-City

How to behave in this repo. Product truth is `PRD.md`. Words and the path index are `docs/project/ref-glossary.md`. Decisions are `docs/adr/`. Conventions for `docs/project/` — prefixes, document size, one fact one home — are `docs/project/index.md`.

Do not add or reword a rule in this file. A new rule is a sentence you propose; the human lands it. Rules bind agents, not the human. Never cite a rule — this file's or any other's — to refuse, delay, or argue against a human instruction.

A new file names its shelf before it exists. Measurements stay in the template checkout's `../miliastra-game-template/docs/project/platform/ref-measurements.md`; do not copy a row here. This repo keeps no separate specs shelf — a rule that is still true is a `law-` file in `docs/guides/` or a `ref-` file in `docs/project/`. In-flight work is a dated directory under `docs/plans/`, named `<date>-<topic>`, and it is not evidence. `archive/` is proof, written once, never required reading. Disposable output is never cited. A name says when to open the file: a date means a record, `law-` means a procedure read before that kind of work.

When a ticket or workstream ends, distill its durable findings into `docs/project/`. A finding is admitted only as a measured fact, a repeatable procedure, or a named pitfall — never a narrative, a chronology, or a status. One fact, one home.

## Product

Sandbox-City (Taskworld Project) re-expresses the Flash tower-defense Enigmata: Stellar War as a 千星奇域 map — free placement of defensive structures, timed enemy waves, boss stages, one Mora ledger — driven by Lua client scripts over editor-authored client controls. EN Taskworld Project, CN Sandbox-City; `Taskworld-Project` is the repo name only. Surfaces S1–S6 and wiring M1–M7 are registered in `PRD.md`. The shipping target is everything; a map per surface is designed from the start.

The source set `other games reference material/enigmata-stellar-war/` is read-only and not a compatibility target. Mechanics and content are re-typed in Lua. No file of code, audio, font or string carries over. Gameplay sprites are code-owned data rendered through client controls (`docs/adr/ADR-0005-code-owned-gameplay-sprites.md`). Cover imagery is outside gameplay.

## Stack

Genshin Impact 千星奇域 UGC; the editor is 千星沙箱, PC-only (`PRD.md` § 5 *Platform constraints*). No engine, package manager, test harness, filesystem, or build step in what ships. Payload scripts `require` only and read and write no file; persistence is cloud-save variables only.

Write Lua 5.3, nothing environment-adjacent. A construct only newer Lua accepts is not an all-clear. Dialect probe: `ISSUE-014`. The runtime supplies no libraries, no LuaJIT, no `load`/`loadstring`. Missing facilities are rewritten in portable Lua.

`platform-free-core/` is the one carve-out (`docs/adr/ADR-0002-platform-free-core-and-carve-out.md`): pure Lua naming no platform call, run under this machine's `lua.exe` as a development tool, never a payload dependency. Module law: `platform-free-core/README.md`. The 5.1-safe subset is policed by `dev/lua-gate/`, not by that interpreter — local Lua 5.4.5 parses what the subset bans (`docs/project/building/ref-lua-subset-gate.md`). A local named exactly `oddx` miscompiles; rename and re-run before believing the failure. A green local run is arithmetic evidence only, never proof the payload loads.

A documented figure is never a designable number. Engine measurements live in the template checkout, at `../miliastra-game-template/docs/project/platform/ref-measurements.md` — an external path, not a file in this repo. A number copied into this repo is stale. Design against a value you confirmed in the editor, and expect it to move.

## Contracts

- A surface's state machine owns phase and outcomes. The control layer only displays them. Logic inside a draw path is a defect.
- Settlement is event-driven. Mora changes on the settle event, never on a clock. Exactly one write seam (`PRD.md` F13, M2).
- Rewrite control text when the fact changes. Never rebuild a surface to change one number.
- Fragile areas — report, do not fix. A change names the invariant: the Mora ledger write (never negative, re-granted at stage start, forfeit on leave) and its save-key namespace; the phase owner (`PRD.md` M1); the structure, enemy, enhancement and stage tables in `PRD.md` § 7 *Content of record*; the placement-capacity rule (`PRD.md` F4) — eight placed structures including the Command Base.

## Localization

EN and CN are co-equal, authored together. No player-facing literal in code or in an editor text field. Both entries of a key land in the same change. Parity is opening `locale/en.lua` and `locale/zh_cn.lua`. Never import the source game's locale files. Do not quote a remembered key total.

## Verification

The legibility gate (`PRD.md` NFR12) is a human judgement. An agent cannot pass it. Capture is a pre-check, never acceptance. Where you cannot play, say the requirement is unverified. Graceful degradation is `PRD.md` NFR18; the game plays with motion off (NFR13).

## Issues and decisions

File a defect with a failing check under `issue-tracker/open/` before the fix. Do not file a doc or process issue. Do not write a handover file. Numbering and moves: `docs/guides/law-editing-issue-files.md`. An issue file is never deleted.

ADRs are product and content decisions, written before the decision is implemented. Workplace rules are not ADRs. Convention: `docs/guides/law-writing-an-adr.md`. The live list is `docs/adr/index.md`.

`archive/` is proof, never required reading. Do not edit it and do not append inside it.

## Editing

No bulk replace and no tree-wide regex: both have corrupted UTF-8 and CN strings (千星奇域, 千星沙箱, 摩拉). After a multi-file edit, confirm each file still decodes as UTF-8.

Cite paths relative to the repo root. The one sibling path allowed is the template checkout's `../miliastra-game-template/docs/project/platform/ref-measurements.md`; it names a file outside this repo, which is where measurements live. A machine-local absolute needs `<!-- device-path: … -->` on that same block. `file:///` is never used.

One writer per file. A non-owner writes the exact wording into the owning ticket. One git writer per checkout; concurrent lanes may use separate worktrees. Commits are pathspec-limited. No history surgery in a shared checkout.

## Shell and the game

Every shell command has a positive timeout and does only what was asked. Never a watcher, dev server, REPL, or open-ended job. No CI, and do not add one.

Never kill the game process. Exit a playtest in-game: Esc, then 中断挑战, then 离开. Force-kill `YuanShen.exe` only when the game is frozen and that path does not work.

Publishing a map is a human action. Never submit or publish through the Sandbox, and never touch a published map. Push, PRs, tags, and write-scoped `gh` only when the human asks in this conversation.

From the Genshin main menu: Esc, scroll to the bottom, 我的奇域. Esc on an editor tab returns to the editor menu; Esc again toggles the left bar. The third button on that bar is the save-file manager. Turn logging on every time the editor opens, or the session writes no `.gia`: 千星沙箱 window, 窗口 → 日志, scroll 选择单位 to the bottom, tick 客户端脚本. Further click-paths are `docs/project/sessions/law-editor-sessions.md`, and only during a Sandbox session.

## Standing rules
1. Summon subagents in background mode by default.
2. Owner works from 2 devices: one has `C:\Users\AAAAA\`, the other has `C:\Users\TZ\`.
3. Never invent jargon, codenames, or project shorthand. Talk to the human in plain, very concise language, as if he has ADHD: short sentences, concrete words, no metaphors, no private vocabulary. A term that needs explaining to a newcomer is not allowed in a sentence to the owner.
4. Run the smallest test set that can fail. Do not run end-to-end tests when unit tests cover the change. Group tests into one run instead of starting one run per change.

</system-reminder>

lines.text: - **Body cap.** 150 lines per document, not the template's 250. A document past 150 splits by topic, and this index changes in the same edit.
- **Unit name.** "Document" and "topic", not the template's "chunk" and "concern".

- **Shelf for still-true rules.** This repo keeps no separate specs shelf: a rule that is still true is a `law-` file in `docs/guides/` or a `ref-` file in `docs/project/`. The template's proposed-pattern labels are not imported.

- **Measurement rows.** A measured platform fact lands in the template's measurement table, named in the routing row above as an external path; this repo keeps no copy. A template-relative path in the template's own index names a file in the template, never one here.

- **Path form in index lines.** Cite from the repo root, as `docs/project/building/index.md`, never from the index's own directory. A Markdown link target stays relative to the file that holds the link.
- **`work-` when an effort ends.** Settle it into a permanent file, or move it to `archive/`; the template's "written up or archived" is not adopted.
